388YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: Senators were returned for Holberg, Karsk, Mareave, Mournwold, Reikos, Sarangrave, Segura and the Barrens. The Senate appointed ambassadors, an Imperial Spymaster, an Advisor on Orc Affairs and several generals. The Synod elected cardinals, inquisitors and many religious stewards, with Hazelelponi taking the Lepidean Librarian title on 312 votes. The Military Council named the Imperial Fleet Master, the Imperial Huntsmarshall and the Strategos of Highguard. Conclave orders chose grandmasters, the Archmage of Spring and Gloaming Sentinel were declared, and the Bourse saw titles auctioned and voted, including Custodian of the Assayer's Guild for Javor de Holburg on 856 votes.

n.Dawn: The Barrens, held by Dawn, returned Lady Gwendoloena de Ordraig as its senator.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave, held by the Druj at the time, still saw an Imperial senator, Bartimaeus, elected for it.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, held by the Grendel at the time, still saw an Imperial senator, Pathfinder Gaddak, elected for it.
n.Highguard: Highguard saw Solomon elected Senator for Reikos, and the Military Council appointed Arlandria of the Sentinels Tower as Strategos of Highguard.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura, held by the Brass Coast, returned Ana i Taziel i Riqueza as its senator.
n.The League: Holberg, held by the League, returned Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg as its senator.
n.The Marches: Mournwold, held by the Marches, returned Mel Bleak as its senator.
n.Varushka: Karsk, held by Varushka, returned Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost as its senator.

t.Holberg: Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg was elected Senator for Holberg.
t.Karsk: Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost was elected Senator for Karsk.
t.Mareave: Pathfinder Gaddak was elected Senator for Mareave, though the territory was held by the Grendel at the time.
t.Mournwold: Mel Bleak was elected Senator for Mournwold.
t.Reikos: Solomon was elected Senator for Reikos.
t.Sarangrave: Bartimaeus was elected Senator for Sarangrave, though the territory was held by the Druj at the time.
t.Segura: Ana i Taziel i Riqueza was elected Senator for Segura.
t.The Barrens: Lady Gwendoloena de Ordraig was elected Senator for the Barrens.

388YE Spring Equinox Military Council or.d: Six armies went to Mitwold, led by the Drakes' Overwhelming Assault and the Golden Sun's Grinding Advance, to reopen Meade, now walled by the Jotun. Five armies took up Solid Defence of Sarangrave to shield the Mallum septs from the Vallorn's Greentide and the Druj Snake and Crane armies. In Mareave, the Summer Storm and Towerjacks defended while the Wolves of War and Argent Sword plundered the Grendel. The Northern Eagle worked to isolate Lower Saarnath ahead of a planned advance. Elsewhere, armies guarded Kallavesa against Fjorknae, raided and rested in Madruga, and many rested in Semmerholm, Zenith, Ossium, Bastion and Upwold.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun made a Grinding Advance into Mitwold behind the Drakes, while the Eastern Sky and Lions of Adelmar returned home to defend Semmerholm and the Gryphon's Pride, under new general Sebastián Fawnwood, defended Ossium.
n.Druj: Three Imperial armies vowed to break the Druj Snake and Crane armies in Sarangrave, and the Northern Eagle set out to cut off Druj garrisons in Lower Saarnath.
n.Grendel: Grendel forces in Mareave faced two defending Imperial armies and plunder by the Wolves of War and Argent Sword, who aimed to strip them of their property and supplies.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar defended Sarangrave against the Vallorn, the Valiant Pegasus tended the fallen in Mitwold, the Pilgrim's Defiance resupplied at Virtue's Rest and the Seventh Wave rested in Zenith.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm returned to defend Mareave from the Grendel, the Winter Sun withdrew to rest in Zenith and the Autumn Hammers made an Arcane Consolidation in Mitwold.
n.Jotun: Six Imperial armies moved against the Jotun-held walls of Meade in Mitwold, the Strong Reeds lay low in Jotun-held Bregasland, and two armies guarded Kallavesa against a Fjorknae attack.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns defended Nesustak Forest in Sarangrave against the Vallorn's Greentide, while the Quiet Step rested and prepared in Zenith.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs raided the Siroc Bayou to begin retaking Madruga, the Fire of the South gave ground in Lightsea, and the Burning Falcon resupplied in Upwold.
n.The League: The Towerjacks defended Mareave alongside the Imperial Orcs, while the Wolves of War plundered Grendel baggage there to fund a later fight against the Broken Shore.
n.The Marches: The Drakes led an Overwhelming Assault to reclaim Meade in Mitwold, the Bounders watched the passes in the Mournwold, the Strong Reeds lay low in Bregasland and the Tusks defended Kallavesa.
n.Urizen: The Argent Sword plundered the Grendel in Mareave to reclaim Imperial Orc property, while the Citadel Guard defended Sarangrave against the remaining Druj armies.
n.Varushka: The Boyar's Hasta and Golden Axe defended Sarangrave against the Vallorn and Druj, while the Northern Eagle worked to isolate Lower Saarnath.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks recovered the lost and the Green Shield fought with honour in Mitwold, while the Narwhal's Spear guarded the gates of Kallavesa against Fjorknae.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar marched from Astolat to Sarangrave.
t.Bastion: The Pilgrim's Defiance resupplied at Virtue's Rest in Bastion.
t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds lay low in Jotun-held Bregasland to harry the Jotun, while several other armies left the territory for Mitwold, Kallavesa, Madruga, the Mournwold and Upwold.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs set out from Feroz to raid Madruga.
t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Kallavesa prepared for a possible attack from Fjorknae.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the Bloodcloaks marched from Hahnmark to Mitwold.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' general recalled their thirty years holding Holberg's walls.
t.Kallavesa: The Tusks took up Solid Defence and the Narwhal's Spear guarded the gates of Kallavesa against any attack from Fjorknae.
t.Madruga: The Red Wind Corsairs made a Daring Raid on the Siroc Bayou while the Fire of the South gave ground in Lightsea.
t.Mareave: The Summer Storm and Towerjacks defended Mareave while the Wolves of War and Argent Sword plundered the Grendel there.
t.Mitwold: Six armies converged on Mitwold to retake Meade: the Drakes' Overwhelming Assault, Golden Sun's Grinding Advance and Green Shield, with the Valiant Pegasus, Autumn Hammers and Bloodcloaks in support.
t.Mournwold: The Bounders watched the passes in the Chalkdowns, guarding the Mourn while the Tusks were away.
t.Ossium: The Gryphon's Pride took up Solid Defence of Ossium to rest and recuperate under its new general.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War, Argent Sword and Black Thorns all marched out of Redoubt, from which the slavers had fled.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Northern Eagle worked to isolate Lower Saarnath, preparing for an Imperial invasion the following season.
t.Sarangrave: Five Imperial armies took up Solid Defence of Sarangrave to protect the Mallum septs from the Vallorn's Greentide and to break the Druj Snake and Crane armies.
t.Semmerholm: The Eastern Sky and Lions of Adelmar returned home to defend and rest in Semmerholm after a year in the Mallum.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks marched from Spiral to Mareave.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance left Therunin, remembering its fallen there.
t.Upwold: The Burning Falcon made a Desperate Reinforcement in Upwold to rest and recover.
t.Zenith: The Seventh Wave, Winter Sun and Quiet Step all took up Solid Defence of Zenith to rest and recover.

r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Fire of the South gave ground in Lightsea to rest at Quzar, keeping watch on the sea.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: The Red Wind Corsairs raided the Siroc Bayou to recover lost Freeborn wealth and begin retaking Madruga.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Bounders watched the passes in the Chalkdowns, hunting brigands and Red Walder.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath: The Northern Eagle set out to tear down bridges and block roads and passes to isolate Lower Saarnath's Druj garrisons.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Black Thorns defended Nesustak Forest and its Mallum septs as the Vallorn's Greentide descended.

388YE Spring Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1726 thrones. The Senate acknowledged the Axou claim to Thornfen, subject to Urizen veto, and abrogated the Astral Arcanist. It created the Herald of the Throne of Glory and established the Cat's Graces sodality. It ratified a treaty returning the Spice Gardens of Feroz and declared that Nesustak Forest belongs to its rebels. Nine Senate commissions were enacted; a tenth, the Barrens Roads, lapsed. Announced works included the Delev Grand Market and several Hahnmark sinecures. Ambassadors were appointed to Otkodov, the Commonwealth, Faraden and the Sumaah Republic. The Imperial Spymaster authorised a raid on Leen and a Thule survey venture, and the Guerdon was set at 350 thrones.

n.Dawn: The Senate created the Herald of the Throne of Glory, appointed by the Dawnish Assembly, to organise the Dawnish National Assembly and crown the Monarch of Dawn. The Senate also commissioned the Mournwold expansion of the Breadbasket.
n.Druj: The Senate declared that the Nesustak Forest rebels had risen against the Druj by their own strength and named a conjunction to treat with them. The Spymaster ordered the smugglers' cove in the Druj-held Salt Flats of Sanath decommissioned after the raid on Leen.
n.Highguard: Cyrus of Ebon's Hall and Accalon of Highguard were appointed Ambassadors to the Commonwealth and the Sumaah Republic. Highguard's Lepidean Librarian began research into a possible new Varushkan exemplar.
n.Navarr: The Wisdom of the Tenebrous Path gained responsibility for guiding the Thorns of Navarr against eternals and other denizens of the realms. A Vallornguard Mustering Ground was commissioned in Holtford, Miaren.
n.Thule: The Spymaster authorised work with the Karass, letting military units survey Thule attempts to claim a Black Lotus plant. The surveying venture received shares of the Imperial Guerdon.
n.Urizen: The Empire conceded the Axou claim to Thornfen, including the Tower of the Skink, subject to a possible veto by the Urizen assembly. Xanthius Storm's End of Urizen became Guildmaster of the Artisans, and the Architects of Urizen self-funded the Eye of Heavens in Zenith.
n.Varushka: The people of Karov self-funded the Golden Bee Assayer's Office and the Delev Grand Market in Duzekani. Highguard's librarians were set to research Kvetmir Kvetmirovic as a possible new Varushkan exemplar.
n.Wintermark: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark became Ambassador to Otkodov, and three new sinecures were announced in Hahnmark: the Garden of Peaceful Quietitude, Spooner's Rest and Runesmith's Caution. The Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq's remit was extended to aid those fighting the horrors of Tsirku.

t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Imperial Spymaster announced that the smugglers' cove here would be decommissioned after the raid on Leen over the coming season.
t.Tsirku: The Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq was given the added responsibility of supporting and aiding those who fight the horrors of Tsirku.

388YE Spring Equinox Synod judgements.d: The General Assembly updated the Doctrine of Seven by greater majority and proscribed Theism, Realmism, ritual death offered to inhuman powers, labyrinth-spirit veneration and preaching against the Virtues, while excommunication with consent was decriminalised. A usury proscription failed. Many assemblies named highest callings, from the Grand Inspiration of the Way to Asavea, the vallorn and damaged territories. Priests urged aid for Therunin's refugees against Agramant, marked six years since the Black Plateau woke, and welcomed the Hallowed Bells pilgrimage. Mandates eased foreign units into Tsirku's wastes and let Dawn and Wintermark raise military units freely. Appointments included new Cardinals of Ambition and Vigilance, and the Virtue Fund made six rewards.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly condemned the Whisper Gallery, called knights to quest into the Untrod Groves once the Manticore is destroyed, and made aiding all nations against the vallorn its highest calling. A mandate let Dawnish resource owners convert to military units at no cost, and a Way Assembly rebuke of Dawnish 'Vengeance' failed.
n.Druj: The Courage Assembly made it its highest calling to study and counter Druj auras of fear and spiritually liberate the Sarangrave septs from their captors. Other judgements spoke of ending the buruk tepel's tyranny and offering refuge to Nesustak's septs.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: 22 thrones went to citizens who sacrificed to catch Grendel spies, a scheme foiled by three traitors, and a withdrawn judgement listed the Grendel among western-front foes.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly urged its chapters and units to aid Navarri refugees fleeing Therunin and honoured the 20 Pilgrim's Defiance soldiers who fell defeating a vallorn abomination. It also called for reparations to the Imperial Orcs, mourned Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum and shaped plans for the Grand Inspiration of the Way.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Knott's words entered the Annals of the Ancestors and Firesong Galath became Guide to the Lost. The orcs pledged to join Varushka and Wintermark in Tsirku, Skywise Rykana was sent to seek lore of the Great Forest Orcs' ancestors, and Highguard's priests called for reparations to them.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's priests cited reclaiming every slave the Jotun took in Sermersuaq, raiding Skallahn and breaking the Gates of Kierheim, and a Marcher friar noted the Jotun's repulse from the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: Navarr's mandate sent Teleri Thornweaver to rally Navarri support for the League's Vallornguard, backed by a Loyalty mandate. The assembly also urged Navarr to shelter Therunin refugees from Agramant, honoured the Pilgrim's Defiance, warned against threats to the Great Forest Orcs and asked Miaren's citizens to tend their bees.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn mandates celebrated profit-seekers, trailblazers and the firebrands' legacy, while the assembly backed the Burning Agora, trade with Morajasse and parleys with Heralds. Highest callings to defend the borders and enshrine contracts passed without the greater majority they need, and the Sail Bell proposal failed.
n.The League: The League Assembly made drawing new peoples into the League its highest calling and welcomed Navarri aid for the Vallornguard. It also welcomed the Tribunal of the Silver Flame's help mapping the City Below, backed a Bill of Mortality and encouraged its orcs to explore hearth magic for reaching the ancestors.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Desilav Sergeyvich Jesen was praised for strengthening trade links with the Thule through tax cuts and food convoy routes.
n.Urizen: Urizen's assembly called its stargazers to seek weaknesses in the Sarangrave vallorn, offered refuge to the septs of Nesustak and accepted Silver Flame help mapping the City Below. Its veto of Thornfen's relinquishment to Axos failed, and a writ was granted for a flame on the docks of Elos.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly celebrated five years of a free Ossium, praised Mayra Zoronova Prochnost's support against the face-peelers and named Armand Remislav to destroy the Sumisev Peegel regio. A Highborn mandate was enacted to stop the decline of southern Varushka's bees, and the nation backed Wintermark's push into Tsirku.
n.Wintermark: Eisa Iron Lungs was entered into the Chronicle of Heroes, and Wintermark mandates eased other nations' units into the wastes, sent Sermersuaq's provisions to the Tsirku scouts and let owners raise military units freely. Priests also challenged the Agramant cultist Kaarina White-Eye, and the Speaker of the Crows election ended in a tie.

t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is named in Mayra Zoronova Prochnost's commendation for backing the campaign against the face-peelers there, and its counting house received a Virtue Fund donation.
t.Madruga: The Vigilance Assembly declared that the tomb of the Ravadi Founders' Dance should be built in Madruga, where they made their last sacrifice and won their eventual victory.
t.Reikos: A writ of consecration to Vigilance for an edifice in Broken Ride honouring the Sodality of the Silent Bell was not upheld, and a Virtue Fund donation was recorded at the Reikos counting house.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: a donation to the Virtue Fund was recorded at the counting house of Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: A Wintermark mandate diverted surplus from the Smokehouse of Atalaq to supply the Tsirku scouting network, at a cost to Sermersuaq's farms. Wintermark's priests also challenged Kaarina White-Eye, a ringleader of the Agramant cults most active in Sermersuaq.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: a donation to the Virtue Fund was recorded at the counting house of Tassato.
t.Therunin: Several assemblies urged help for Navarri refugees fleeing Therunin, so Agramant cannot pose as their only rescuer. Priests honoured the Pilgrim's Defiance soldiers who fell against a vallorn abomination there and looked to a day when Therunin is Navarri again.
t.Tsirku: A Wintermark mandate cut the penalty for units from other nations scouting or exploring Tsirku's wastes from three ranks to one, and Sermersuaq's provisions were committed to the scouting network. Varushka and the Imperial Orcs backed the exploration.

r.Reikos/Broken Ride: A writ of consecration to Vigilance was sought for the new edifice in Broken Ride honouring the Sodality of the Silent Bell, built with white granite from the Virtue Fund and Bryce the Hare, but it was not upheld.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: The Highborn Assembly asked that, once the vallorn infestation of East Ashes is cleared, the remains of the 20 Pilgrim's Defiance soldiers who fell there be recovered for the Stewards of the Dead.

388YE Spring Equinox event schedule.d: Eight nations elected senators on Saturday afternoon in their own camps: Segura, The Barrens, Reikos, Mareave, Holberg, Mournwold, Sarangrave and Karsk. Tally of the Votes elections for national titles followed from 3:30pm for Highguard, Navarr, Varushka, the Imperial Orcs, Urizen, the Brass Coast, the League and Wintermark. The timetable listed Senate sessions, Military Council sessions, Field Marshal briefings, Conclave sessions, Synod deadlines and the Saturday and Sunday battles. It also included citizen-organised gatherings such as a Forum on the Iron Confederacy, a Weirwater Forum, Vallorn war discussions, the Tourney for the Rose Throne and a meeting of Hahnmark farmers.

n.Dawn: Dawn elected the senator for The Barrens at 2:30pm on Saturday, immediately after the tourney, and the schedule included a Dawnish Fleet Captains' Meeting and the Tourney for the Rose Throne.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but the Sarangrave they held had its senator chosen by Urizen.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are not named, but the Mareave they held had its senator chosen by the Imperial Orcs.
n.Highguard: Highguard began its inquisition of candidates for the Reikos senator at 2:00pm and held Tally of the Votes elections in the Chapel for the Bursar of the House of Spirits, the Exarch of Virtue's Rest and the Steward of the Ossuary.
n.Imperial Orcs: Candidates for the Mareave senator began presenting items of worth at 2:15pm, and the Fire Pit hosted elections for the Steel Fist, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post and the Sorrowful Tunnels.
n.Navarr: Navarr held a Tally of the Votes election for the Broker of Thorns at the Standing Circle at 3:30pm, with the next regular election due at the Winter Solstice 388YE.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast opened its auction for the Segura senator at 1:00pm and elected the Broken Shore Bounty, the Cerevado Nets and the Dhomiro of Afar at the Waypoint.
n.The League: The League elected the Holberg senator through the presentation of collected bonds at 3:30pm and chose the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild at the Plaza.
n.The Marches: Landowners of the Marches gathered at 1:30pm to elect the senator for Mournwold.
n.Urizen: Urizen held a demos for the Sarangrave senator from 1:00pm to 1:30pm and elected the Architect of Hammers. The schedule also included a Urizen Magician's Meeting and the Challenge of the Boards in the Urizen camp.
n.Varushka: Varushka began questioning candidates for the Karsk senator at 1:45pm and elected the Gift of the Dwindling Star, the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore and the Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks at the Central Hearth.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark elected the Mediator of Wreck, the Talon of Kauppahall and the Mediator of Fisk at the Tree of Names, where a meeting of Hahnmark farmers was also held on Saturday evening.

t.Hahnmark: A meeting of Hahnmark farmers was scheduled for 6pm on Saturday at the Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp.
t.Holberg: The League elected Holberg's senator on Saturday at 3:30pm through the presentation of collected bonds.
t.Karsk: Varushka elected Karsk's senator on Saturday afternoon, with the questioning of candidates beginning at 1:45pm.
t.Mareave: Although Mareave was held by the Grendel, the Imperial Orcs elected its senator, with candidates presenting items of worth from 2:15pm.
t.Mournwold: The Marches elected Mournwold's senator when landowners gathered at 1:30pm on Saturday.
t.Reikos: Highguard elected Reikos's senator on Saturday, beginning with an inquisition of candidates at 2:00pm.
t.Sarangrave: Although Sarangrave was held by the Druj, Urizen elected its senator through a demos held from 1:00pm to 1:30pm.
t.Segura: The Brass Coast elected Segura's senator by auction, beginning at 1:00pm on Saturday.
t.The Barrens: Dawn elected the senator for The Barrens at 2:30pm on Saturday, immediately after the tourney.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: a Weirwater Forum appeared on the Friday evening timetable.

388YE Spring Equinox interlude.d: The 500-throne Guerdon went to units supporting the Argent Sword, Drakes, Eastern Sky and Narwhal's Spear. Military units were offered ventures to aid the Thule Earthquake Drummers invading the Forest of Ulnak, to root out trudnik in Karsk and Ossium, to fight threats in Spiral, and to exploit the espionage ring in Sarvos. Fleets could escort Sumaah aid to the Brass Coast. Congregations could investigate Sarvos, support the Pilgrim's Defiance, or encourage pilgrimages to Capodomus and Hacynian. Rivers of Life, Frozen Citadel, Dripping Echoes, Regrow the Land's Heart and a Day projection over Sermersuaq were in effect, alongside Marcher and League economic mandates.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units were among those eligible to join the Swords Against Darkness venture against the threats in Spiral.
n.Druj: The Druj faced a Thule assault on the Forest of Ulnak led by the Earthquake Drummers, which Imperial warbands were invited to join, while the Eastern Sky in Sarangrave drew Guerdon support.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel luxuries were among the rewards of the Exploit the Espionage venture, and Grendel-held Feroz and Mareave were listed among enchanted lands.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations could preach Vigilance to investigate Sarvos for traitors or forgo liao to support the Pilgrim's Defiance against the vallornspawn in Therunin.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs appeared in the monstering table at 96%, and Mareave, which they partly held, was warded with Frozen Citadel magic.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: only through Bregasland, which they held, where units supporting the Narwhal's Spear shared in the Guerdon.
n.Navarr: The Pilgrim's Defiance fighting the vallornspawn in Therunin could be bolstered by Highborn congregations, with ten reducing casualties and twenty increasing territory taken.
n.The Brass Coast: Delayed Sumaash aid bound for the Brass Coast was readying to sail, and the more Imperial fleets escorted it, the more white granite the House of the People would risk sending.
n.The League: League units could fight in Spiral and League congregations investigate Sarvos, while a League Assembly mandate let Leaguers convert resources to businesses freely and upgrade businesses more cheaply until Spring 389YE.
n.The Marches: Units supporting the Drakes in Mitwold shared the Guerdon, Mitwold was under Rivers of Life, and a Marcher Assembly mandate let Marchers convert resources to farms and upgrade farms more cheaply.
n.Thule: The Thule invited Imperial warbands to join the Earthquake Drummers' assault on the Druj in the Forest of Ulnak for mana crystals, and the Claws of the Dragon worked with Varushkans against the trudnik.
n.Urizen: Urizen units could join the Spiral venture, units supporting the Argent Sword in Redoubt shared the Guerdon, Redoubt was enchanted with Rivers of Life and Tomari with Frozen Citadel, and no new rituals entered Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Varushkan units could raid trudnik lairs in Karsk and Ossium, at the cost of a production penalty for draughir there, while Ossium was enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq was flooded with Day magic, Hahnmark was enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart, West Marsh in Kallavesa received Dripping Echoes of the Fen, and Wintermark fleets gained a rank trading at Caitun.

t.Bregasland: Military units supporting the Narwhal's Spear in Bregasland were among those sharing the Imperial Guerdon.
t.Feroz: Feroz was woven with Rivers of Life, reducing army casualties there and infusing its waters with restorative Spring power.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Thule Earthquake Drummers were pushing into the Forest of Ulnak against the Druj, with Imperial warbands invited to join for a reward of mana crystals.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark was enchanted with a Llofir-infused Regrow the Land's Heart, turning ruins to gardens and giving farms and herb gardens magical mushrooms in place of some of their usual yield.
t.Kallavesa: The West Marsh region of Kallavesa was enchanted with Dripping Echoes of the Fen by the Sussivari Frost Coven.
t.Karsk: Varushkan units could join the Thule in hunting trudnik nests in Karsk, though suspicion would impose a production penalty on Karsk's draughir.
t.Mareave: Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was cast on Nadir by Phoenix Rising and on Clisearn by Ashen Flame.
t.Mitwold: Units supporting the Drakes in Mitwold shared the Guerdon, and the territory was woven with Rivers of Life.
t.Ossium: Trudnik lairs in Ossium, one apparently very old and extending into the earth, could be raided, at the cost of a penalty to draughir, while Regrow the Land's Heart overgrew its war-scarred lands.
t.Redoubt: Units supporting the Argent Sword in Redoubt shared the Guerdon, Rivers of Life lay over the territory, and Tomari was enchanted with Frozen Citadel.
t.Sarangrave: Units supporting the Eastern Sky in Sarangrave shared the Guerdon, and the territory was woven with Rivers of Life.
t.Sarvos: If at least 30 congregations investigated Sarvos, the espionage ring might be uncovered via the Sentinel Gate, though Sarvos taxes would fall by four thrones, while units exploiting the ring made investigation harder.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was flooded with Day magic, easing entry for Day realm inhabitants and turning minds towards intellectual rather than physical pursuits.
t.Spiral: The Swords Against Darkness venture offered the chance to bring Spiral's threats under control, and if sustained it would permanently raise taxation by six thrones and remove the Black Plateau penalty to military units.
t.The Barrens: The Hope's Rest region of the Barrens was enchanted with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by Phoenix Rising.
t.Therunin: The Pilgrim's Defiance fought the vallornspawn in Therunin, and congregation support could reduce its casualties and increase the ground it took.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: West Marsh was enchanted with Dripping Echoes of the Fen by the Sussivari Frost Coven.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn was enchanted with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Ashen Flame coven.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Nadir was enchanted with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Phoenix Rising coven.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Tomari was enchanted with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Ashen Flame coven.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Hope's Rest was enchanted with Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae by the Phoenix Rising coven.

388YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Twenty-six winds were released. Among them were appraisals on the Cat's Graces sodality, Livardz, the Nesustak rebels, Tsirku and the Beurteilung, and highest callings for Highguard and Navarr. Others covered the Earl of the Groves' tourney claim to the Rose Throne, the Karass, the bees of Karov, face-peelers, Redoubt after the Grendel withdrawal and Sarangrave's miasma pillars. Diplomatic winds covered eleven foreign powers; the Grendel remained at war and pushed into Mareave. Other events included the disputed Tassatan Hills seat, Hope's Rest becoming rimebound, the Crown of Three Tears being withheld, the Marcher Assembly's defence of Marcher orcs and a failed Vigilance investigation in Sarvos. Results of four major and thirty-four minor conjunctions were also listed.

n.Dawn: The manticore Earl of the Groves claimed to be Monarch of Dawn, and Dawn's nobles must fight a tourney to decide who, if anyone, sits on the Rose Throne. Dawnish magicians of the Phoenix Rising coven also made Hope's Rest rimebound.
n.Druj: Emperor Vesna readied the Empire for a final push to end the Druj. Druj forces were defeated or cleared at Camp Askoun Orama, Skinflawed's Corral, Hywel's Track and Greensward Lea, and Grettek Skinflawed was killed.
n.Grendel: The Grendel remained at war, abandoned Redoubt, launched a major push into Mareave with Asavean support, and made no formal diplomatic contact. Their suspected espionage ring in Sarvos escaped exposure, while their raiders had mixed results against Imperial heroes.
n.Highguard: Highguard turned to completing the Grand Inspiration of the Way as its highest calling. The Highborn Assembly's peerless kinship offered hope of returning bees to Karov, and the Beurteilung academics reported on ties with the Commonwealth.
n.Imperial Orcs: An Imperial Orc Assembly expedition successfully learned of the Karass ancestors. The Black Tillers offered a Garden of Hope great work in Skarsind, and the Marches pledged to defend Marcher orcs against any Synod proscription.
n.Jotun: The Jotun remained at war with the Empire while their ambassador's hetjuveisla and a Loyalty consecration of the meeting place were pursued. Ghodi Uksahkka reached Kierheim, the Tromsdalen fyrd formed, and Eluf Asbjørnsson survived to raise Greenwall's fyrd.
n.Navarr: Navarr's highest calling to aid Urizen and the Vallornguard bore results, and the Glimmerwater steading agreed to relocate to Miaren. The Greenwatcher title was reinstated without powers.
n.The Brass Coast: With the Freeborn lands no longer immediately threatened, Anduz in Segura sought new opportunities. The Protectorate of Morajasse made a fidelitous offer, and wreckers in Madruga were defeated.
n.The League: The Chamber of Euphony in Apulian was completed, and the Forge and Furnace Fellowship demanded the Tassatan Hills be restored as a League seat. A League and Highborn Vigilance investigation into Grendel spies in Sarvos was thwarted.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly's pledge to defend Marcher orcs opened a Preach Pride action for congregations. At Two Barrel Field Bill of Beatsdown was killed and Jim Moor murdered, but Stephen of Sarcombe survived.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov remained at peace with the Empire and appointed a new ambassador, while focusing on their invasion of the Forest of Ulnak. Their Claws of the Dragon worked with Varushkans against face-peeler nests.
n.Urizen: Urizen faced rebuilding in Redoubt after the Grendel fled and the Tower of Light and Shadow was broken. Its seers reported on countering Sarangrave's miasma pillars, and Navarr's highest calling brought aid to the nation.
n.Varushka: Varushka received an appraisal on restoring Livardz after the Cold Sun attack, and saw the fallout of raids against the face-peelers. Highborn kinship offered a chance to return the lost bees of Karov.
n.Wintermark: The mystics of Ishal advised on scouting Tsirku, and the Crown of Three Tears was withheld until Wemba the Bloody and Kaarina White-Eye are slain. Hahnmark was offered deeper ties with Sarcophan merchant families.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The Thule of Otkodov have turned their focus to invading the Forest of Ulnak, though little is known of the campaign.
t.Hahnmark: Two Sarcophan merchant families offered farm and herb garden owners deeper relations. Valdr Grieversonn agreed to meet Eevi of the Gadrai, and people of Hahnmark were touched by strange magic.
t.Hercynia: Strange rumours at Starwood Roots Steading were investigated by the Archmage of Winter. Hercynia, where Ravadi first fought the vallorn, was also proposed as a site for their tomb.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's senator was advised on the Tassatan Hills dispute, and Holberg was listed among possible homes of units involved in the Sarvos counter-espionage.
t.Kallavesa: Coral husks were destroyed at Ingrid's Rock in the West Marsh.
t.Karov: The bees of Karov, missing since the Blade of Skies appeared, might be restored through the Highborn Assembly's peerless kinship.
t.Madruga: Wreckers were defeated at Draws Sward and the House of Guerra was protected on Corsair's Road. Madruga, where Ravadi died, was also proposed as a site for their tomb.
t.Mareave: The Grendel launched a major push into Mareave while Beoraidh explored diplomacy with the Empire. Fleisardh gained the coastal quality after its conjunction went untaken.
t.Miaren: The Glimmerwater steading agreed to relocate from Eastring to Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: people from Miekarova, especially mine owners, were tagged as interested in the strange magic described in Ripple of echoes.
t.Mitwold: At Two Barrel Field Imperials fought the Wayford Traitors: Bill of Beatsdown was killed, Jim Moor was murdered and three items of worth were lost. Mitwold's inhabitants were also warned of awry Imperial magic.
t.Morrow: Wreckers were defeated on Xavier's Path, and Disciples of Sulemaine were slaughtered on the path to Highwatch. The Three Watchers fortification was reviewed for renewal.
t.Mournwold: At the Hare Stone, Linley Weaver answered the call of Warrenwise and solved the problem.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the people of Ossium were tagged as interested in the strange magic described in Ripple of echoes.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov stayed at peace with the Empire under a new ambassador, and cultural works of storytelling were exchanged at Leopard-Tooth Pass in Sküld.
t.Redoubt: After the Grendel fled, Redoubt weighed what to do with the Tilphussian Reach where the Tower of Light and Shadow stood, while southern Redoubt suffered from awry magic. Grendel and Disciples of Sulemaine were defeated in Siluri, Tomari and Limus.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Joran of Reikos led the Highborn Vigilance investigation in Sarvos.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: people interested in Reinos were tagged in the Iron Confederacy diplomatic wind.
t.Sarangrave: Urizen seers reported on targeting the keystone miasma pillars, and an appraisal began on the Nesustak Forest rebels. Druj were defeated in Thornfen and Whisperwood.
t.Sarvos: Highborn and League priests failed to expose a suspected Grendel espionage ring in Sarvos. Wreckers were defeated at Antonio's Glebe, and the Library Scriptorium was protected from Cinders.

t.Sermersuaq: Agramant's cultists Wemba the Bloody and Kaarina White-Eye still threaten Sermersuaq, but the Ceaseless Hunter, the Feasting Lord and coral husks at Scop's Lookout were destroyed.
t.Skallahn: Ghodi Uksahkka reached Kierheim unopposed and the Tromsdalen fyrd formed, while Eluf Asbjørnsson survived to raise Greenwall's fyrd. Imperials defeated a construct bound for Kierheim and rescued the crew of the Old Jim's Ewe.

t.Tassato: The Forge and Furnace Fellowship demanded the Tassatan Hills ilium seat be returned to the League or that they be invited to discuss terms.
t.The Barrens: The Earl of the Groves claimed the Dawnish throne, the Karass offered suggestions to aid the Empire, and Hope's Rest became rimebound. Barrens resource owners were invited to make their holdings rimebound too.

t.Upwold: Cinders were killed and Benson's Orchard protected at Benson's Bawn.

t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater, where Ravadi was born, was suggested as one possible site for their tomb.

388YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The Grendel stirred in the Bay of Catazar and fought on in Mareave. The Jotun had invaded Mitwold and looted Meade, while Imperial forces sought to retake Bregasland, centred on Gravenmarch. In Therunin the Pilgrim's Defiance marched against the vallorn of Tharunind, and the Empire advanced on the Tower of the Skink, the last Druj stronghold in Sarangrave. The Military Council would pick two of five battles: two in Sarangrave, and one each in Mareave, Mitwold and Bregasland. Conjunctions included miasma pillars in Sarangrave, ettercap threats near the vallorn, and Lasambrian and Jotun raiders. The page also listed nation-specific military considerations and force weights.

n.Dawn: Dawn carried a force weight of 63, its armies could not use Cautious Advance or Give Ground, and the Druj needed 25 victory points to claim a beachhead in the patrolled Barrens. Slaying the ettercaps in Brocéliande would boost Dawnish units questing against the vallorn.
n.Druj: The Druj held the Tower of the Skink as their last Sarangrave stronghold, depleted but unbroken, and were the foe in both Sarangrave battle opportunities. A band of Kallad led other Druj through Drownbark Forest after retreating from Thule invaders.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were said to be scheming around the Bay of Catazar and still pressing in Mareave, where a battle opportunity to freeze their advance was offered at Ohwinn Scour.
n.Highguard: Highguard carried a force weight of 27 and could use Protect the Innocent, but would suffer penalties for herald-boosted armies and gain bonuses attacking Zenith from Morrow. Conjunctions in Reikos and Casinea dealt with refugees, ettercap-captured Highborn and the rescue of Mendicant Garev.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs were listed with a force weight of 7 for the battle muster.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had invaded Mitwold, looting Meade, and occupied Bregasland, though the Mournwold had slipped from their grasp. Lasambrian and Jotun warbands featured in conjunctions in Hahnmark, Sermersuaq and Reinos.
n.Navarr: Navarr, with a force weight of 60, saw the Pilgrim's Defiance fight a hopeless delaying war against the vallorn of Tharunind in Therunin. Ettercap threats emerged in Hercynia and Brocéliande.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast carried a force weight of 17, and conjunctions in Feroz and Madruga called on its titles to reclaim the Brazen Links, stop the Hand of Dumon and slay dire astacids.
n.The League: The League carried a force weight of 23 and was tasked with conjunctions to claim the Vorlach Adventurers' wage in Spiral and stop the Hand of Dumon in Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Marches suffered the Jotun invasion of Mitwold and the sack of Meade, while the Empire fought to retake Bregasland. Marcher armies could not Give Ground but gained home-territory bonuses, and any Imperial army could Billet in Marcher lands.
n.Thule: Thule armies invading the Forest of Ulnak had driven a band of Kallad south-west, and a conjunction sought to recover Thule material in Grimfen Mire.
n.Urizen: Urizen carried a force weight of 12. Morrow and Zenith were patrolled so that the Druj needed 25 victory points for a beachhead there, and Urizen armies attacking Zenith from Morrow gained bonuses.
n.Varushka: Varushka carried a force weight of 17 and could use Hospitality of the Boyars in patrolled Ossium. Conjunctions spread across Karov, Karsk, Ossium and Volodmartz.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark brought the largest force weight, 71, and gained honour-based modifiers against the Jotun. Its titles were charged with conjunctions in Hahnmark, Sermersuaq and Kallavesa.

t.Madruga: A conjunction in the Crucible tasked the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield with slaying dire astacids.
t.Mareave: Armies clashed under the Wide azure skies along a coast reshaped by the sea, and a battle opportunity was offered to freeze the Grendel advance in Clisearn.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold had been invaded for the first time in centuries and Meade conquered and looted. A battle opportunity and a conjunction sought to recover Meade's treasures, and the Drakes gained strength here.

t.Ossium: Kallad were leading Druj through Drownbark Forest towards Shchaslyvyy Outpost, and strange wagon raiders were to be investigated. Ossium's patrolled borders meant the Druj needed 25 victory points for a beachhead.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the battlefields and mountains of Redoubt appeared only in the poetic opening.
t.Reikos: Conjunctions tasked heroes with assisting refugees at an emergency hospital in High Chalcis and rescuing Highborn captured by ettercaps near Chalcis Mount.
t.Reinos: A conjunction at Beatriz's Field in Bastasor called on the Champion of Ambition to claim the Lasambrian banner.

t.Spiral: A conjunction at Broken Lea in Apulus tasked the Oblivion Sentinel with claiming the wage of the Vorlach Adventurers.

t.Therunin: The Pilgrim's Defiance marched against the vallorn of Tharunind to slow it, and ettercaps were carrying Highborn captives back towards Therunin.

t.Volodmartz: Conjunctions sent cadets to destroy a bandit vale in Murupa and others to end the suffering of the Shadow Fellowship in Livardz.
t.Zenith: Zenith's borders were patrolled against Druj beachheads, and Highborn and Urizen armies attacking into Zenith from Morrow gained bonuses.

A bright cerulean flame.d: Accompanied by nearly five thousand mostly Navarr soldiers, the Pilgrim's Defiance swept aside Druj traps and defenders, encountered heralds of the Agramant slaughtering Druj, and reached Mudlark's Haven, where failed Druj warding obelisks left the orcs besieged by vallornspawn. Two dozen volunteers died destroying a unique abomination fused with a miasma pillar that spread terror. The army then withdrew to Lustri. The vallorn is now quiescent; East Ashes is infested but unclaimed, Mudlark's Haven remains Druj, and Therunin is nominally Druj. Highborn congregations may support the army until Summer 389YE. Separately, refugees freed by the Agramant's servants have overwhelmed the hospital at High Chalcis, offering a relief opportunity.

n.Druj: Druj forces in East Ashes were routed by the Pilgrims and ravaged by the vallorn and Agramant's heralds, yet clung on to Mudlark's Haven and keep nominal but feeble control of Therunin; their failed warding stones and a possible Buruk Tepel hand in the pillar-abomination raise questions.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Pilgrim's Defiance lost around 1,500 soldiers but halted the vallorn in East Ashes, an inspiring feat that lets Highborn congregations keep supporting the army until Summer 389YE.
n.Navarr: Navarr soldiers and vates marched alongside the Pilgrims to save their homeland, though centuries of Navarr work reclaiming the marshes were partly undone and Navarr refugees freed by the Agramant's servants fled to Reikos.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the army marched across Urizen's Zenith, past memorials to the Highborn armies that defended Urizen from the Druj.

t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Three Watchers memorial stands over the pass into Morrow.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: other Imperial soldiers were pressing south in Redoubt while the Pilgrims marched east.
t.Reikos: Refugees led out of Therunin by the Agramant's servants overwhelmed the hospital at High Chalcis, whose healers asked the Medical Officer of the Pegasus Respite to bring a team of physicks through the Sentinel Gate.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: trapped Druj could only flee upriver to the Salt Flats by passing through another vallorn.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Druj fleeing across the Feverwater would find only Imperial steel or Nesustak rebel spears in Sarangrave.
t.Therunin: Therunin saw the Pilgrims check the vallorn's expansion, which has now subsided into quiescence; the territory remains nominally Druj but largely belongs to the beasts of the marsh.
t.Zenith: The Pilgrim's Defiance marched through Zenith, taking anointings beneath the Three Watchers, and afterwards regrouped in Lustri to count its losses.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: the Druj obelisks at Mudlark's Haven were modelled on the Terunael warding stones of Bendol.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Mentioned in passing: Nesustak rebels' spears await any Druj fleeing into Sarangrave.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: East Ashes was saved from being claimed by the vallorn but is now infested, with vallornspawn equivalent to a 4,000-strong force in its western and northern reaches, while the Druj still hold Mudlark's Haven.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring, already lost to the vallorn, poured vallornspawn husks onto Mudlark's Haven and now blocks safe passage between East Ashes and the Lower Tarn Valley.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Lower Tarn Valley cannot be reached from East Ashes without crossing the vallorn and suffering casualties, and it remains poisoned.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: the Druj at Mudlark's Haven were battling the abomination of the Sweetglades.
r.Zenith/Clypion: The Pilgrims marched through Clypion past the Three Watchers, where many soldiers were anointed with liao donated by Highborn congregations.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The Pilgrims passed through Iteri beneath the Three Watchers memorial, where many took anointings before the campaign.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The army crossed Lustri past the ruins of the Stork's Gaze, then fell back to its Night-haunted woods to regroup and keep watch northward.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: the army marched through Proceris, where the Golden Cascade flows once again.

A knock at the door.d: Ehsan, Lord of Sand, welcomed the Senate's choice of an ambassador (Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard) without an embassy, which helps protect Beoraidh's neutrality. He appointed his great-nephew Rubhart Kaltrin in return. Beoraidh renewed its offer of land for a temple or basilica of the Way, with halved labour costs if an orc commissions it. It also renewed a dock investment and proposed a salt-for-beef trading post with the Unshackled. It offered to arrange a meeting with the Brine Turtles if the Senate facilitated an introduction to Skoura, and refused to spy for either side. Warlord Bikk proposed a mandate enabling reaver ventures against the Brine Turtles, though Unshackled voices disagreed.

n.Grendel: Beoraidh refuses to spy on the Grendel for the Empire, insisting on strict neutrality. Ehsan offered to spend his favours with his former Grendel peers to arrange talks with their Brine Turtles sept.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Beoraidh, Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, is Highborn.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orcs were offered cheaper construction of a temple or basilica of the Way in Beoraidh, and the Unshackled a salt-for-beef trading post. The national assembly was asked to back Warlord Bikk's mandate for reaver raids on the Brine Turtles, amid disagreement among the Unshackled.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark maggots would be welcome to join the proposed raids on the Brine Turtles, and Bikk hoped Winterfolk reavers would attend the discussion at Anvil.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: with the Children of Wrecks apparently on the way out, Beoraidh may be able to fish the bay's waters again.
t.Mareave: Beoraidh balances between the Empire, the Grendel and the Sarcophan Delves while fighting continues across the territory. Reavers proposed raiding the Brine Turtles sept to cut army supplies or drive them out.
t.Skarsind: If the proposed salt-for-beef trading post were built, the Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind would gain 5 extra crowns each season from access to Beoradhi salt.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The city-state appointed Rubhart Kaltrin as ambassador and renewed offers to sell land for a temple of the Way and to take dock investment. It ruled out spying for either side and left any formal colosseum invitation to Imperial warbands on hold.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Mentioned in passing: refugees from wealthy Clisearn swelled Beoraidh's population during the war.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal was offered as a site for the Unshackled trading post on the Sinfoyard border. Beoradhi access to its Grand Aqueduct reportedly requires Skouran agreement.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Brine Turtles sept of Fleisardh is the proposed target of reaver raids. If enough force joined the plunder venture, many of the sept would withdraw south to Grendel-protected lands.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Warlord Bikk moved his Legion to Icarion to coordinate the proposed raids, and Icarion was offered as a site for the salt-for-beef trading post.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Sinfoyard forms part of Ehsan's planned neutral state, and Beoraidh proposed building its matching trading post on the Sinfoyard side of the border. A temple of the Way would preach to its orcs.

Alongside the Earthquake Drummers.d: At the invitation of the dragon Tathenon the Gyre, Imperial captains mustered in the southern Webwood with the Earthquake Drummers under Saemundr Elvirsbairn and four other Thule armies. The drummers' loud advance drew the Druj to battle in the haunted, miasma-shrouded woods of Oerwealt, where the Thule and over two thousand Imperial troops defeated a Druj ambush of perhaps ten thousand. The Thule then turned toward the Great Pit in the Bonewall but were slowed in the hills. The Jaws of Winter Lightning laid a sickness curse across Ulnak and awakened Oerwealt's trees. Imperial units were paid in crystal mana, and the same pay of seven crystal mana per unit was offered for further service.

n.Druj: The Druj lost Oerwealt and most of the Bonewall, and their garrisons at Cassad Ûln and the Thistle of Barbs took heavy losses, though both bastions remain untouched. Unless their armies respond, the Great Pit is expected to fall by the Summer Solstice.
n.Thule: Otkodov's armies, guided by the Dragons, claimed Oerwealt and are poised to besiege the Great Pit. The Eyes of the Dragon, who serve Hinodir of the Bright Orb, were seen searching the forest for something unknown.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named; it is linked only through Ossium, where the Thule armies mustered.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Thule recalled their role in liberating Sermersuaq, and the Banner of the Rime Hound's war rhinos were remembered from the Battle of Ikka's Tears.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The Thule conquered Oerwealt and pushed deep into the Bonewall. Ritual magic now curses the coming season with a sickness that will raise casualties among armies and garrisons fighting there.
t.Ossium: Ossium served as the mustering ground for the invasion. The Thule noted that they had sent warriors to help conquer it and had hoped the Empire would return the favour.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the invading Thule are identified as the orcs and armies of Otkodov, whose astronomancers name the Wanderer "the Eye of Chaos".
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the main Druj armies were concentrated to the south in the Salt Flats and Sarangrave rather than in Ulnak.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Thule pointed to their part in Sermersuaq's liberation as a reason the Empire might aid them.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi is not named on the page; it is linked only as Thule-held land.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: Mentioned in passing: Ghul'thak Forest is not named; the campaign concentrated on Oerwealt and the Bonewall.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: The Thule conquered Oerwealt's haunted woods after defeating a large Druj ambush. Spring magic awakened its trees to protect the Thule and harry any Druj attempt to retake it.
r.Forest of Ulnak/The Bonewall: The Thule took about three-quarters of the Bonewall but were slowed by Druj fighters using caves and tunnels. They are ready to besiege the Great Pit, which scouts expect to fall by the Summer Solstice unless the Druj respond.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The armies mustered in the southern Webwood, where Thule warlocks have woven a Spring ward that makes the trees attack intruders. Many old Druj traps and deadfalls remain uncleared in its deeper parts.

Amend Virtue's Respite.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Tassato, the motion amended an existing sinecure in Hanuri at a cost of 30 crowns in labour and three months of work. The title, appointed annually by the League National Assembly and providing four liao and seven crowns each season, was renamed from Guardian of Giselle's Tomb to the Bloody Custodian of Pride. Funds came from several citizens, chiefly Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar, who gave 2 thrones 6 crowns. On completion, citizens of Temeschwar with congregations could take the Preach Pride - Pride of Temeschwar lecture until the Winter Solstice 388YE. It produces no liao but grants two extra Synod votes.

n.The League: The League National Assembly gained an annually appointed title, the Bloody Custodian of Pride, worth four liao and seven crowns a season. League citizens of Temeschwar paid for most of the work.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's senator proposed the amendment to the city's monument. Its citizens with congregations could then preach the Pride of Temeschwar lecture for two extra Synod votes until the Winter Solstice 388YE.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Virtue's Respite in Hanuri was reworked into the Bloody Massive Pride of Temeschwar, and its guardian's title was renamed the Bloody Custodian of Pride.

An arrow nocked and in flight.d: The Protectorate holds Mora's Rock with veteran orcs and Wind Lord Saoirse, a master of Sand lore. Its attempts to buy supplies from the Freeborn of Feroz and Segura have largely failed because of memories of Governor Rahab's tyranny. Gallum agreed to meet at the Summer Solstice after Garviel i Abrira i Erigo and Khalil i Carno i Guerra offered safe passage. His proposal, open until the end of that Solstice, would return the Spice Gardens to Imperial control and restore the Keeper of the Spice Gardens as a Freeborn national title appointed by the Imperial Apothecaries Guild. An optional appraisal could use the Protectorate's engineers to help Feroz. The civil service warned of possible espionage risks, and noted the Freeborn assembly could support or sink the deal.

n.Grendel: The Protectorate is treated as foreign and separate from the Grendel for as long as it stays independent, though the civil service suspects some contact with the Salt Lords. The Silent Bell is also preparing a report on Grendel espionage rings around the Bay.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn could regain the Spice Gardens and a restored Keeper title, but only if their farmers agree to feed the orc garrison. Their national assembly holds the power to encourage or effectively sink the arrangement.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell is investigating Grendel espionage rings across the wider Bay, and the Spice Gardens are noted for growing some of its finest Cerulean Mazzarine.
t.Feroz: The long-fallow Spice Gardens of Feroz could return to Freeborn hands, and an appraisal might help rebuild the territory's prosperity, its bridges across the Scorrero or its defences. However, its people remain wary of the orcs who once enforced Rahab's rule.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Gallum expects the Iron Confederacy matter concerning the islands of Madruga to be settled by the Summer Solstice.
t.Segura: Some Freeborn of Segura are prepared to trade food with Mora's Rock despite widespread suspicion. Any appraisal could look for ways for the orcs to work with the people of Segura.

r.Feroz/Morajasse: Morajasse remains held by Gallum's Protectorate from the fortress of Mora's Rock, with its borders largely closed. Under the proposal its supply troubles would ease and travel restrictions on Imperial citizens would be relaxed.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: the battle at Oran is cited as the point after which the Senate recognised the Protectorate.

Archive:Roll of Honour Spring Equinox 38.d: The roll lists each supporter's name, nation, home territory and banner against the force or operation they backed. Armies and fleets supported included the Argent Sword, Black Thorns, Boyar's Hasta, Citadel Guard, Drakes, Golden Axe, Granite Pillar, Northern Eagle, Red Wind Corsairs, Strong Reeds, Summer Storm, Wolves of War and the Will of the Wintermark. Spy networks were also supported: Defence of the Broch, the Forest of Ulnak and, most heavily, Tsirku. Fifty Wintermark citizens from Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, among them many of Dunhearth Hall and the Shield Wolves, plus one Navarr, backed the Tsirku network. The Drakes and Black Thorns drew especially broad support.

n.Dawn: Dawn's nobles gave widespread support, above all to the Drakes, where House Orzel and House Mortére of Weirwater stood out, and to the Black Thorns. Others backed the Boyar's Hasta, Granite Pillar, Argent Sword, Red Wind Corsairs and Summer Storm.
n.Highguard: Highborn citizens backed the Drakes, among them members of The Steel Tide from Necropolis, as well as the Argent Sword, Granite Pillar, Summer Storm, Black Thorns and Northern Eagle. Silus of The Sentinels Tower supported the Forest of Ulnak spy network.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orcs of Mareave and Skarsind threw their weight behind the Summer Storm and the Argent Sword. Bands such as the Irontide, Bloodcrows, Sand Vipers, Pathfinders and Stonesworn were prominent among them.
n.Navarr: The Navarr overwhelmingly supported the Black Thorns, with many striders from Hercynia, Miaren and Brocéliande, and also backed the Argent Sword, Drakes, Boyar's Hasta and Summer Storm. Powell Open-Skies also aided the Tsirku spy network.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast citizens from Feroz, Kahraman, Madruga and Segura supported the Red Wind Corsairs, including members of the Bloodgold Jackals and Flames of the Coast.
n.The League: A handful of League citizens contributed. Two from Temeschwar backed the Argent Sword, Gunter Von Holberg supported the Drakes, and Pierra di Sarvos of the Crimson Reaper Cartel supported the Wolves of War.
n.The Marches: Marchers from Upwold, Mitwold, Mournwold and Bregasland mainly supported the Drakes, notably The Talbots, The Fire of the Marches and the Applewood Levy. Rowan Gotts backed the Strong Reeds and Bradwin Barlymaine the Red Wind Corsairs.
n.Urizen: Urizeni citizens supported the Argent Sword and the Citadel Guard, including members of the Scythe of The Sarangrave. Others backed the Summer Storm and the Red Wind Corsairs.
n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens backed the Drakes, largely through the Grimhold Guard, as well as the Argent Sword and Summer Storm. Kazimiera Radovna Suvretzska was the sole listed supporter of the Golden Axe.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark dominated the roll. Fifty of its citizens supported the Tsirku spy network, Siegfried Eofogar backed the Defence of the Broch network, and Mandrake Lightfoot supported the Will of the Wintermark. Many Dunhearth Hall members also backed the Drakes.

t.Tsirku: Tsirku was the focus of the season's largest spy network effort, supported by fifty Wintermark citizens from Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq and one Navarr.

Arranging grace.d: The Court judged the manifesto 'elegant and concise' but ruled that the Maestro could represent the sodality, not lead it. Approval would move titles such as the High Bard of the Empire and the Dean of the First Voice Glade to election by the sodality. The Mistress of Monuments would follow unless the Senate redefined it around the inspirations. No existing powers would transfer automatically, and the sodality would be singular. The songbirds offered to fund the refinement of commissions. League princes and Highborn benefactors pledged grants to a patrons' fund. Some artists criticised the name. The Senate established the sodality with power to refine a commission and to preserve chosen artworks in First Voice Glade. It set a one-throne stipend, creating a Patron's Fund of five thrones a season.

n.Highguard: Highborn benefactors joined League merchant-princes in pledging three thrones a season to the sodality's fund and in matching any Senate stipend, provided grants were disbursed openly.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the walls of Damata are cited as an example of a historical commission the sodality might refine.
n.The League: League merchant-princes, led by Genia Bourné di Sarvos, pledged funding to the sodality. Diora University was named as a possible repository for honoured art, and il Volpe's League galleries and theatres were held up as a model of arts patronage.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the scops' halls of Kalpaheim were listed among possible central repositories for the sodality's honoured artworks.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the many basilicas of Bastion are cited as historical commissions the sodality could ask artists to refine.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim's scops' halls were suggested as a possible repository for the sodality's art, though First Voice Glade was ultimately chosen.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the walls of Damata are given as an example of a historical commission open to refinement by the sodality.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Genia Bourné di Sarvos, merchant-prince of the Bourné fashion house, acted as spokesperson for the patrons pledging funds to the sodality.

r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Mentioned in passing: the walls of Damata are cited as an example of a historical commission the sodality could refine.

Bricks and boards.d: Entrants must be the target of the Summer ritual Challenge the Iron Duke; four covens, three Dawnish and one Wintermarker, cast it the previous season. The Challenge of the Boards was a four-round tourney of fifteen-minute two-player strategy games, each round a different game, with at least one Summer herald competing and the top half of the table victorious. It was held at the House of the Wanderer camp in Urizen at 16:00 on Saturday. The Challenge of the Oaken Bricks pitted Imperial teams of up to four against a foreign team from Otkodov, Kalsea and Narkyst at kubb in the Anvil arena at 14:00, with each game winner-takes-all.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: three of the four covens that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season, Phoenix Rising, the Cabal of Nevezamzer and the Coven of Golden Wings, were Dawnish.
n.Jotun: Jotun kubb players from Kalsea and Narkyst were to come to Anvil under escort of Barien's heralds, as part of a foreign team taking on Imperial challengers at a game played in their winter homelands.
n.Thule: Thule players from Otkodov were to join the foreign kubb team at Anvil, competing in their own challenge of the Iron Duke against Imperial teams at a game the Thule play in their homelands.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the strategy games tourney was to be held at the House of the Wanderer camp in Urizen, arranged through Revel.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Voices of the Unbound Storm, a Wintermark coven, was one of four that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

t.Otkodov: Otkodov, held by the Thule, supplied players for the foreign kubb team that was to travel to Anvil to challenge Imperial competitors in the arena.

Chain and anchor.d: The Buidelrat and deBruin accepted that the Empire did not want their offers. Jakhalsmarkt access continues until the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Sarcophan visitors were warned to respect Imperial law after the Hester van de Moerassen affair. League and Freeborn citizens attended the Alivetti celebration, but Highguard stayed away, so the Delves will make no approaches to Highguard for a year. After the Senate limited the Apothecaries' Guild to Imperial citizens, the Kruidenkenner withdrew most offers and proposed a cooperation appraisal. The Highborn stone trade ended and the Cathedral of the Navigators lost most of its ministries. Marieke of the House of the Maggot offered 140 Thrones for it, available only at the Spring Equinox.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the page notes only that the Sarcophan have extended protection to the independent city-state of Beoraidh in Mareave.
n.Highguard: Highborn heeded Exarch Aemon's statement and stayed away from the Alivetti celebration, so the Delves will make no approaches to Highguard for at least a year. The lucrative stone trade has ended and the Cathedral of the Navigators has lost all but one rank of its merchant ministry, with an offer made to buy the building.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn attended the Alivetti revels in numbers, and their business owners gained a free diversification. Ambassador Dino i Riqueza was praised for his patience, and Freeborn figures such as Estrella and Guild Leader Esmé i Estrico i Erigo are tied to the cooling Kruidenkenner relationship.
n.The League: League citizens attended the Alivetti celebrations openly and in good numbers, and their business owners gained a free diversification from deals struck during the revelry.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bay appears only in a further-reading link to an earlier wind about growing Sarcophan influence there.
t.Madruga: Business owners in Madruga received consumables from the Alivetti estates, some possibly illegal in the Empire, as goods flowed out of the celebration.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the overview notes that the Sarcophan have extended their protection to Beoraidh in Mareave, apparently to guarantee its neutrality.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is not named; the page refers only generally to Highborn businesses and mines losing their stone-trade profits.
t.Sarvos: The Sarcophan enclave at the Alivetti estate in Sarvos held its week-long five-year celebration, and local business owners received consumables from it. Selling the Cathedral would have no implications for the enclave.
t.Tassato: Business owners in Tassato received consumables from the Alivetti estates after the celebration, and magistrates will struggle to stop illegal goods entering the Empire.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh is named as an independent city-state now under Sarcophan protection to help guarantee its neutrality.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named; the page refers only generally to Highborn mines and businesses losing their stone-trade income.

Construct Beoraidh Trading Post.d: The commission followed the A knock at the door Wind of Fortune and was described as fully funded. It cost 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour, plus standard costs, and took three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Sandviper Nid supplied 3 thrones, 5 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams gave 1 crown. Once finished, the Beoraidh Trading Post raised the income of the Shepherd of the Southern Herd by 10 crowns each season and that of the Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind by 5 crowns each season. It also secured trade between the Unshackled and Beoraidh.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is attached only because it held part of Mareave, where the trading post was built.
n.Imperial Orcs: The trading post, built in Icarion in Mareave and commissioned on the Mareave senator's proposal, increased the seasonal incomes of the Shepherd of the Southern Herd and the Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind.

t.Mareave: A new trading post was built in Mareave's Icarion region to exchange salt for beef with neighbouring Beoraidh, adding 10 crowns a season to the Shepherd of the Southern Herd's income.
t.Skarsind: The Shepherd of the Great Herd in Skarsind gained 5 extra crowns each season from the completed trading post.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Beoraidh became the trading partner for the new post, supplying beef in exchange for salt, and its trade with the Unshackled was secured.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Icarion was chosen as the site of the Beoraidh Trading Post, which was built there with weirwood and crowns from Imperial donors.

Construct Cerulean Balmhouse.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Zenith, the commission created the Cerulean Balmhouse, a herb sinecure whose holder is elected by the Freeborn National Assembly and has tenure. The motion drew on the aid of the Sumaah Republic offered through the Forging Links wind of fortune, as part of ongoing co-operation. Construction required standard costs, 20 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, reduced because Fontargenta was impoverished, and took three months. After the Spring Equinox, Mont i Sawa i Erigo provided 1 throne 2 crowns and the 20 wains of weirwood, and Sumaah citizens provided a further 1 throne 2 crowns. The Freeborn Assembly would appoint the first Herb Tender at the Summer Solstice 388YE.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion and is linked to it only because it held part of Feroz that season.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a new tenured herb sinecure in Feroz, with the Herb Tender of the Cerulean Balmhouse to be elected by their National Assembly from the Summer Solstice 388YE.

t.Feroz: Feroz gained a new herb sinecure, the Cerulean Balmhouse, built in Fontargenta with Sumaah support while control of the territory was divided between Grendel and the Brass Coast.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Fontargenta became the site of the Cerulean Balmhouse, and its impoverished state lowered the labour cost of the construction to 20 crowns.

Construct City of Wonders.d: The edifice cost 50 wains of white granite, 35 of weirwood, 5 of mithril, 30 rings of ilium and 270 crowns in labour, and takes six months to build. Brass Coast citizens supported it through mandates enacted by Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo, Isario i Riqueza and Val, and the Cat's Graces provided the foundational artwork, created by Karrak. Many contributors supplied materials and money after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice. Once complete, it creates the Burning Agora, a new southern propylaeum, a restored Market of a Thousand Sails and an enchanted Fountain of Wonders. It also adds the Firebrand, Hawker and Trailblazer Freeborn archetypes and changes Anduz's fate to become the City of Wonders.

n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn citizens backed the project with mandates and contributed most of the materials and coin. The completed edifice gives the Brass Coast three new archetypes, the Firebrand, the Hawker and the Trailblazer, and promises wealth, adventure and new ideas.

t.Segura: Segura's city of Anduz is to be transformed into the City of Wonders, with a restored Market of a Thousand Sails, a new propylaeum and the Burning Agora for the exchange of ideas.

r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Anduzjasse is the site of the six-month construction. Once complete, it gains the torchlit Burning Agora, a southern propylaeum, the restored Market of a Thousand Sails and the enchanted Fountain of Wonders at the city's centre.

Construct Delev Grand Market.d: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, announced the great work and described it as time-sensitive. It required 50 wains of white granite, 150 crowns in labour and three months to build. Between Spring and Autumn 388YE, donors including Blazh Zbignev, Triska Markova and Nikolai Yaropolk Borislav contributed 50 wains of granite and coins in total. Once complete, the market would raise investment in Karov's businesses, give citizens a free year's business there, and improve the Iron Tower, Korotny Docks and Delev Market. Karov's taxes would rise by four thrones a season, but only if the Little Boyar's Welcome were also upgraded. The Senate could also let the Boyar of the Iron Roads create a sinecure each season.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens led the effort. The market promises Varushkans more profitable businesses in Karov, including a year of free business ownership, and lets the Boyar of the Iron Roads gain a sinecure through Senate motion.

t.Karov: Karov's people offered to fund a grand market in Delev that would raise business investment in the territory. It would also improve the Iron Tower, Korotny Docks and Delev Market, and could add four thrones a season to Karov's taxes if the Little Boyar's Welcome were upgraded too.

r.Karov/Duzekani: The grand market was to be built at Delev in Duzekani, and by Autumn 388YE donors had supplied the full 50 wains of white granite it required.

Construct Eye of Heavens.d: Proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by Feroz, the motion was to be fully self-funded by the Architects of Urizen. It required 30 wains of mithril, 20 of white granite, 10 of weirwood and 225 thrones in labour, with six months to complete. Recorded contributions were small: a crown each from Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven after the Spring Equinox, and 5 rings in donations after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the observatory would enable study of the stars, conjunctions and astronomancy to rival Spiral's proposed school of dramaturgy, found a new spire letting any Urizen character take a free resource in the territory, and spread one hundred mana crystals through Brass Coast businesses.

n.Urizen: Urizen's Architects undertook to fund the observatory themselves, and on completion its citizens could each claim a new resource in Zenith for free through the new spire it founds.

t.Zenith: Zenith's senator proposed the motion, which would give the territory a major observatory for astronomancy and a new spire once building is finished.

r.Zenith/Occursion: Occursion is the site chosen for the Eye of Heavens, a six-month construction of mithril, white granite and weirwood dedicated to the study of the stars and conjunctions.

Construct Garden of Peaceful Quietitude.d: Hilda Sirens Scream Ursan, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced construction of the Garden of Peaceful Quietitude in Kalpamark, Hahnmark, following the opportunity presented in the Poet lights but lamps wind of fortune. The sinecure cost 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns in labour, and took three months to build. Hilda provided 4 thrones 4 crowns and the 12 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox 388YE. Once complete, it created the tenured title of Seeker of Quietitude, appointed by the Wintermark National Assembly. The Assembly could make the first appointment at the Summer Solstice 388YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new tenured title, the Seeker of Quietitude, which its National Assembly could appoint for the first time at the Summer Solstice 388YE.

t.Hahnmark: The Garden of Peaceful Quietitude was built in Hahnmark, paid for with weirwood and coin supplied by Hilda Sirens Scream Ursan.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: Kalpamark became the site of the completed Garden of Peaceful Quietitude, the sinecure attached to the Seeker of Quietitude.

Construct Golden Bee Assayer's Office.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by the senator for Karov, the motion described the people of Karov as wishing to self-fund the building, and stressed that the opportunity was available that season only. Construction required 14 wains of mithril and 42 crowns in labour, taking three months. After the Spring Equinox Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each contributed a crown. Once complete, taxation from Karov rises by two thrones per season, and a new national position, the Golden Bee Assayer, is appointed by a Tally of the Votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners and receives 5 ingots each of orichalcum, weltsilver and green iron per season.

n.Varushka: Varushka gains a new national sinecure, the Golden Bee Assayer, chosen by the nation's mine and forest owners and receiving orichalcum, weltsilver and green iron each season.

t.Karov: Karov's senator seconded the motion, and once the office is complete the territory's taxation rises by two thrones per season.

r.Karov/Duzekani: The Golden Bee Assayer's Office is to be built in Duzekani, costing 14 wains of mithril and 42 crowns in labour over three months.

Construct Grand Guildhouse of the Printe.d: The project was announced by the Chair of the Wolf rather than passed as an ordinary motion. It required 30 wains of white granite and 90 crowns in labour, and would take three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Jonah Yakovitch provided 11 thrones 2 crowns and the 30 wains of white granite. Once complete, the guildhouse would raise the income of the Curator of the Printers' Guild Museum to 20 crowns a season and of the Custodian of the Printers' Guild Mausoleum to 3 thrones a season. It would also let a key member of the guild spread one publication across the Empire each season for a throne, and let a merchant-prince of the guild make a single address to the Empire after its completion.

n.The League: The League's Chair of the Wolf, Taddea Ginori, announced the grand guildhouse to honour its Printers' Guild. Once finished, it would strengthen the guild's offices and its reach in spreading publications and addresses across the Empire.

t.Tassato: Tassato, held by the League, was chosen to host the Printers' Guild's grand guildhouse, with materials and funds supplied after the Spring Equinox for its three-month construction.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Tassato Mestra is the site of the new Grand Guildhouse of the Printers' Guild, built of white granite as the guild's monument to truth.

Construct Lisabetta Docks.d: The commission cost 75 wains of white granite, 50 wains of weirwood and 375 crowns in labour, with twelve months to complete. The Lijkkever family of the Sarcophan Delves lent their expertise, removing the extra cost of building in a marsh, though they were not granted exclusivity. The Sand Fisher orcs were invited to build a weirwood trade enclave in the new port and donated heavily. Many citizens contributed materials and money through 388YE. Once complete, the docks will raise business and trading-fleet investment in Holberg, boost Semmerlak taxation by 15 thrones a season, found a new coastal town, open a ferry to Ossium, and create a League position, the Prince of the Imperatrix Docks.

n.The League: The League gains a great work in Holberg that, once complete, will raise investment in Holberg businesses and trading fleets, briefly cheapen business upgrades for Holberg citizens, and create a new League position, the Prince of the Imperatrix Docks, with bourse access for Holberg businesses.
n.Varushka: Once the docks are complete, a new ferry across the Nameless River will boost trade between Holberg and Varushkan-held Ossium, and the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore will see purchase prices rise by a tenth.

t.Holberg: Holberg's senator proposed the commission, and its citizens supplied much of the granite, weirwood and coin to build the docks that will found a new town on its coast and make it a trade hub on the Semmerlak.
