t.Ossium: Ossium is to be linked to Holberg by a new ferry across the Nameless River, boosting trade between the two territories, and as a Semmerlak territory it shares in the increased taxation.

r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund is the site of the Lisabetta Docks, a marshland great work that will host a new port town, a Sand Fisher weirwood enclave and offices for the new Prince of the Docks.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore will see purchase prices rise by one tenth once the docks are complete.

Construct Path to the Lyceum.d: The edifice was built as set out in the Sound and Vision opportunity. The announcement gave the cost as 15 weirwood, 5 rings of ilium and 45 crowns in labour, self-funded by the Dean of the Lyceum. The recorded costs list 15 wains of weirwood, 5 rings of ilium and 15 crowns in labour, reduced because of the impoverished nature of Fontargenta, with three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Syl supplied the ilium and weirwood. Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund each gave 5 crowns 10 rings, and Bakar i Riqueza gave 4 crowns. The completed Path to the Lyceum restored the connection between Oranseri and the Lyceum.

n.Grendel: The Path was raised in Oranseri, part of Feroz, which Grendel held at the time, though the page does not name Grendel or give it any role in the work.
n.The Brass Coast: The new edifice restored Oranseri's link to the Lyceum in Feroz, a territory the Brass Coast held at the time, though the page does not name the nation directly.

t.Feroz: Feroz gained a completed edifice, the Path to the Lyceum, which restored the connection between Oranseri and the Lyceum.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: the labour costs were reduced because of the impoverished nature of Fontargenta.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Path to the Lyceum was built in Oranseri, and its completion restored the region's connection to the Lyceum.

Construct Runesmith's Caution.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, the commission created a money sinecure teaching rune lore. The school also tells the tale of Wayland, Thane of the Proud Quill, who broke his oath by sharing Runesmith's Law with people of other nations. It was to be self-funded by his friend Cormack Dun Farstrider, editor of The Oathwright, and the people of Wintermark. Cormack Dun supplied most of the 10 wains of white granite and the labour costs, and Rhys Nighthaven gave 1 crown. Once complete, it created the Wintermark national title Dean of Runesmith's Caution. The Dean was first to be appointed at the Summer Solstice 388YE by tally of the votes of Wintermark military unit captains.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Wayland Runesmith's Caution, whom the school commemorates, died fighting the Druj in Summer 386YE.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the commission was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar in his role as Master of Rings.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a rune lore school honouring one of its fallen thanes, funded by its own people. It also gained a new national title, Dean of Runesmith's Caution, chosen by its military unit captains.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark became home to Runesmith's Caution, a white granite school teaching rune lore to artisans of the Mark.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar appears only in the name of the announcing Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: The sinecure Runesmith's Caution was built in Kalpamark and was complete by Summer 388YE.

Construct Spooner's Rest.d: Announced in Spring 388YE by Eldrid 'Phoenix Flame' Vestardottir as Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, the commission created a church celebrating the life and passions of the fabled Tobrytan Dunning, decorated with many golden eagles and yellow suns. Its holder, the Conscience of the Dunnings, advises and guides the Dunning family and is appointed annually, and can be revoked, by the Wintermark National Assembly. The work required 10 wains of white granite, 30 crowns in labour and three months. Eldrid provided 3 thrones 5 crowns and the granite, and Rhys Nighthaven gave 1 crown. The sinecure was completed, with the first appointment due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

n.Wintermark: The Wintermark National Assembly gained a new annual appointment, the Conscience of the Dunnings, which it can also revoke, with the first appointment due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark gained a new liao sinecure, Spooner's Rest, a church honouring Tobrytan Dunning that advises the Dunning family.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Spooner's Rest was built within Dunhearth Hall at Wood Heath, a church adorned with golden eagles and yellow suns.

Construct Statue of Umbar.d: Using her power as Mistress of Monuments, Ada Droon Drifting Bough announced the building of a likeness of Umbar Elba Stado in Madruga. It was to demonstrate his Pride and commemorate virtuous acts verified by individuals across the Brass Coast. The edifice required nine wains of white granite, 27 crowns in labour and three months to build, plus standard costs. After the Spring Equinox, Umbar i Elba Stardo i Guerra himself provided 3 thrones 3 crowns and the nine wains of white granite. The work was finished and a statue now stands in the Lightsea, Madruga.

n.The Brass Coast: A Brass Coast citizen, Umbar Elba Stado, is honoured with a public statue for his Pride and for virtuous acts attested by people across the nation, and he funded its construction himself.

t.Madruga: Madruga, held by the Brass Coast, gains a completed white granite statue of Umbar Elba Stado.

r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Lightsea is where the statue of Umbar Elba Stado was raised and now stands complete.

Construct Vallornguard Mustering Ground.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by Hercynia, commissioned the mustering ground for 10 wains of weirwood, 10 wains of mithril and 60 crowns in labour. It took three months to build and needs no upkeep. The project was self-funded. Kevan Heartsbane provided 10 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of mithril and 5 thrones 6 crowns, and Corwyn Heartsbane gave the other 5 wains of mithril. Drysfa Broken Bough, Eleri Bronwen's Rest, Nathair Autumngale, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven made smaller donations of coin. The Vallornguard would appoint the first holder of the new title at the Summer Solstice 388YE, for a shortened term of nine months.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained a new title, the First Thorn of the Vallornguard, appointed by the Vallornguard, and Navarri such as Kevan and Corwyn Heartsbane paid for its construction.

t.Miaren: Miaren became home to the newly built Vallornguard Mustering Ground, a sinecure for the Vallornguard.

r.Miaren/Holtford: Holtford is the site of the Vallornguard Mustering Ground, completed after three months of construction.

Cup of choices.d: Following Navarr, Loyalty and Urizen assembly mandates in Winter 387YE, Navarri and Urizeni magicians drew up proposals. Mithril Woven Nets in Ventosi would raise Redoubt's mana sites and create the Woven Architect of Crystal to buy mana and sunfruit. Rebuilding Sunspire in Peregro would create the Arbiter of Sunspire, who would receive prismatic ink, and would add a ritual to Urizen lore. The Citadel Guard could adopt the Technique of the Immanent Claw. A Navarr-built Eastern Citadel in Sarangrave would hold a 3,000-strong garrison. Arhallogen offered the Venom Den one last time, but it remains proscribed by the Synod. All were opportunities, not completed works.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units, alongside Urizeni and Navarr ones, could take the Patrol Béantal Dol guarding action if the Eastern Citadel were built, earning rewards like those of a quest against the vallorn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Druj force from Therunin is recalled as having looted and burned Sunspire after the Summer Solstice 386YE.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the mithril nets would protect Ventosi from flooding if the Foam and Spittle curse were used against the Grendel.
n.Navarr: The Navarr shared their centuries of vallorn lore with Urizen and helped design the proposals. These included the Eastern Citadel, a wayhouse whose Bulwark of the East would be a Navarr title, with a mixed Navarr and Urizeni garrison.
n.Urizen: Urizen was offered greater mana production in Redoubt and the chance to rebuild Sunspire, with a new ritual for its lore. The Citadel Guard could adopt a venom-focused technique, and a joint citadel could be built to defend Sarangrave.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Scorpion Queen's offer is made despite the recent saga with the Navarr in Brocéliande.
t.Morrow: Sunspire, burned by the Druj in 386YE, could be rebuilt in Morrow as a sinecure. It would again be Urizen's centre for coordinating action against the vallorn.
t.Redoubt: A proposed great work would raise investment in every mana site in Redoubt by one. Its overseer would also be able to buy mana crystals and sunfruit from the territory's spires.
t.Sarangrave: The Eastern Citadel could be built here, giving the territory a 3,000-strong garrison, a patrol of Béantal Dol, higher taxation and continued magical targeting from the Imperial regio. Arhallogen also offered the proscribed Venom Den here.
t.Therunin: If the proscribed Venom Den were built, Arhallogen's heralds would help Imperial armies inflict extra casualties on the vallorn in Therunin as well as in Sarangrave.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro is the site where Sunspire could be rebuilt, creating the Arbiter of Sunspire title and its prismatic ink income.
r.Redoubt/Ventosi: Mithril nets could be strung across the Ventosi cliffs to strengthen mana flows. They would also shield the region from flooding if the territory were cursed with Foam and Spittle.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Bloodwater Marsh is one of three possible sites for the Eastern Citadel, provided no other fortification stands there.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Turan Flats is one of three possible sites for the Eastern Citadel, provided no other fortification stands there.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Whisperwood could host the Eastern Citadel. It is also the proposed site of Arhallogen's Venom Den, a fane that is currently proscribed.

Deep blue sea.d: The Grendel withdrew from southern Redoubt with few engagements, sailing from Elos after looting spires, ruining the Tower of Light and Shadow and abducting about two dozen arcane scholars, their families, shipwrights, glassmongers and a lightstone cutter. Elos's harbours reopened, though its lightstone obelisks blaze nightly. The Tempest, the Simoom and five Asavean warships raced to Calvos Sound but missed the Red Wind, which became an army again in Feroz and then anchored offshore without attacking. Feroz remained quiet, with the Children of Wrecks driven out. Conjunctions offered fights against Grendel in the Crucible, Spiral and Oranseri.

n.Grendel: The Salt Lords abandoned their conquests in Redoubt, taking captives and loot, while their Tempest and Simoom navies, with Asavean allies, failed to catch the Red Wind Corsairs and lingered at anchor off Calvos; Grendel companies also feature in three conjunctions.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel and Asavean armada sailed past the shores of Necropolis and the watchers of Reumah's Redoubt without attacking.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns, under General Cadwell Waystone, joined the push that drove the Grendel out of Redoubt, framing it as ensuring that Therunin would not fall.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs evaded the Grendel armada, landed at Oran to celebration and became an army again in Feroz, while the Freeborn of Madruga watched an enemy fleet anchored off Calvos Sound that did not strike.
n.The League: The Wolves of War, led by Jean d'Apulian, helped reclaim Redoubt, and in Spiral the Oblivion Sentinel was given the chance to destroy a Grendel mercenary company and claim its pay.
n.Urizen: Redoubt was returned wholly to Urizen hands with the Argent Sword's help, but its spires were looted, the Tower of Light and Shadow devastated, and dozens of Elos's scholars and craftsfolk carried off by the Grendel.
n.Wintermark: The sacrifice of the Fist of the Mountains was credited with saving Elos from destruction, and its recapture opened an opportunity to raise that army's banner in the port in their honour.

t.Bay of Catazar: A combined Grendel and Asavean armada swept through the bay's waters in pursuit of the Red Wind, which deliberately quit the sea to sow doubt in Grendel dominion of the bay.
t.Feroz: The Red Wind Corsairs landed at Oran and became an army again; the Protectorate of Morajasse kept its watch, the Iron Confederacy stayed impassive, the Children of Wrecks were gone, and the Empire retained overall control.
t.Madruga: The Grendel armada arrived in force but, finding the Red Wind gone, anchored offshore without assailing the largely unprotected shores, while a Grendel company sought to camp in the Crucible.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the armada sailed past the shores of Necropolis without turning shoreward.
t.Redoubt: The territory was reclaimed in full as the Grendel withdrew, though its spires were plundered, people kidnapped and the Tower of Light and Shadow ruined, its regio disrupted.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the armada passed through the southern waters of Sarvos, watched by the Chain against Chains, without attacking.
t.Spiral: A Grendel mercenary company hired against Imperial holdings was splintered by the Black Plateau's malignancy, leaving it open to the Oblivion Sentinel.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns' general declared that Therunin would not fall as they marched on the Grendel.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance left the Redoubt foothills and headed north into Zenith to fight other battles.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Iron Confederacy remained in control and impassive, sending civilian ships, perhaps with spies among them, to trade at Feroz ports.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Protectorate of Morajasse remained in the west, its orcs keeping apart from the Red Wind amid tension while honouring their agreement to patrol Feroz's shores.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Red Wind disembarked at Oran to revelry, and the Corsair of Oran was charged with recovering the Brazen Links from the Grendel Silver Runnel anchored near Escambal.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The armada's intended trap closed on empty water; the fleet then rested at anchor off Calvos, showing interest in the municipal docks under construction but not attacking.
r.Madruga/Crucible: The Drakespawn sought to bring a breeding pair of dire astacids into the Crucible, threatening the Camp of the Sand Crab unless the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield killed them.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The armada briefly pushed into the passage off Free Landing, and a dozen pirate vessels from there that harried the fleet were swiftly destroyed.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Red Wind sailed south through Lightsea's coastal waters, and the Grendel pursuit faltered in the narrows off its beaches before turning back.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Elos was retaken and its harbours reopened, but it had been stripped of wealth and kidnapped scholars and craftsfolk, and its lightstone obelisks now blaze strangely each night.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: Three Imperial armies swept through Siluri meeting only brief, one-sided clashes as the Grendel retreated, leaving its spires looted.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Vorlach Adventurers, hired to threaten holdings in Apulus, were broken up by the Black Plateau and left as prey for the Oblivion Sentinel.

Expand Breadbasket into Mournwold.d: Proposed by the senator for Mournwold and seconded by Weirwater, the motion called for 39 wains of weirwood, 19 wains of white granite and 174 crowns in labour costs, with six months to complete. Materials and money came from many contributors after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice, notably Orson BogMyrtle, Mel Bleak, the Alders of Hay and Wayford, and Stockwater Monastery. Once complete, every farm in the Mournwold gains an additional 36 rings each season from the Winter Solstice 388YE, and the Marcher ability to support armies rises by one once Bregasland returns to Marcher hands. The Keeper's Cottage gives the Keeper of the Breadbasket 12 crowns a season.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but the extra Marcher army support depends on Bregasland, which they held at the time, returning to Marcher hands.
n.The Marches: Marcher senators drove the motion and Marcher citizens largely paid for it, gaining richer Mournwold farms, an income for the Keeper of the Breadbasket and, once Bregasland is recovered, the capacity to support one more army.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Breadbasket's boost to Marcher army support only takes effect once Bregasland is back in Marcher hands.
t.Mitwold: The Keeper's Cottage sinecure is built in Mitwold, giving the Keeper of the Breadbasket 12 crowns a season from the Winter Solstice 388YE.
t.Mournwold: The Breadbasket great work is expanded into the Mournwold, granting every farm there an additional 36 rings each season from the Winter Solstice 388YE.

r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: Maiden Downs is the site of the newly built Keeper's Cottage, the sinecure that funds the Keeper of the Breadbasket.

Fear quickens the breath.d: Anka Karass withdrew her treachery allegations against members of her own sept and accepted a transactional relationship with the Empire, backed by the threat of force. She was attacked at the meeting, and the matter is under criminal investigation. Karass scouts confirmed Thule armies attacking the Druj in the Forest of Ulnak. The Imperial Spymaster could authorise a joint venture to survey Thule attempts to claim a Black Lotus. The Karass also proposed that the Senate cede the Last Battle to them, which the Navarr Assembly could veto, in exchange for scouting on the borders. Separately, they offered potions for beggar's lye through the Carmine Fields Trading Post. Illegal potions were surrendered to a magistrate.

n.Dawn: The Karass want the Dawnish investment in the Barrens to turn a healthy profit, and they offered the Envoy potions in place of herbs through the Carmine Fields Trading Post.
n.Druj: The Karass admit they fear Druj vengeance, and their scouts confirmed that Thule forces are attacking Druj lands in the Forest of Ulnak, possibly to seize the Buruk Tepel's Black Lotus plants.
n.Navarr: Ceding the Last Battle would devastate the Navarr of the Barrens, whose steadings and stridings rely on the wayhouse, so the Navarr National Assembly could veto the motion.
n.Thule: The Karass regard the Thule as enemies and offered to help the Empire spy on Thule attempts to claim a Black Lotus. They are unaware that the Thule already know of the Imperial spy network in Ulnak.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Karass scouts confirmed Thule armies attacking the Druj here, and the Imperial spy network could support a joint survey of Thule efforts to seize a Black Lotus. The network is likely to last only a season or two before the Thule destroy it.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov is named as one of the few ways the Thule might learn of the Karass scouting.
t.Sarangrave: If the Last Battle were ceded, the Karass would take over watching the Sarangrave border in place of the wayhouse's projection of Imperial force.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the in-character text recalls a past Druj push into Semmerholm in which Lenna's parents died.
t.The Barrens: The Karass of the Barrens are now cooperating with their Imperial overlords and offering trade. They have also asked for the Last Battle Wayhouse to be ceded to them.
t.Therunin: Rumours of worrying events in Therunin have alarmed the Karass, who offered to watch for Druj movements there if the Last Battle were ceded.

r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: If the Last Battle were ceded, the Spymaster could have the Karass watch the Nesustak Forest rebels and report any changes. The region would remain protected by the Gryphon's Pride watchtowers.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Last Battle Wayhouse stands in the Bleaks, and the Karass are deeply agitated by its presence and want it ceded to them.
r.Therunin/Eastring: If the Last Battle were ceded, Eastring would cease to be under threat, because the Karass refuse to enter vallorn-claimed land. No Imperial army can currently claim the region in any case.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Under the cession proposal the valley would stay under threat, and the Karass offered to study its Druj poison so that it could be cured. That antidote opportunity has since been superseded by another wind of war.

Five flames.d: The Court of the Five Winds welcomed work beginning on Yakholme Grange and the prospect of trade with Dawn. Faraden expected to renew its peace treaty with the Jotun at the Summer Solstice. A true consecration of the Temple of the High Flames, made possible by liao from the Imperial Gatekeepers, weakened Asavean religious influence but cooled Faraden interest in the Way. Ambassador Mistress Singua Karadragha sought assurance that the Synod's new proscriptions on Vengeance, which the Empire holds to be the same as Faraden's flame of Justice, would not apply to Faraden travellers. The Cinders' leaders were tried and executed, including Zuchlagch, who was burned at the stake. The Lictors offered a chamber for Asavean Tommaso Triusti's trial and requested testimony from Imperial Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo.

n.Dawn: The Court of the Five Winds was pleased that Faraden trade with Dawn might be moving forward, and saw that overland trade with the Empire avoided the perils of the sea routes the Asaveans depend on.
n.Jotun: Faraden could not afford war with the Jotun and seemed certain to renew its peace treaty with them at the Summer Solstice, though Mistress Karadragha expected Suranni adventurism to help her nation extract some concessions.

t.Reinos: Faraden lies beyond the Lasambrian Hills of Jotun-held Reinos. Mistress Karadragha's hope that the Empire would join an attack on Reinos came to nothing, as the Military Council's focus lay elsewhere.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the dangers of the Sea of Snow were cited as one reason Faraden merchants prefer overland trade with the Empire to Asavean shipping routes.

Flames and the dark.d: Thanks to Umarth "Winter's Flame" Kannask and the Fist of the Mountains, Elos escaped the worst, and no major Senate repairs were needed. The Grendel instead looted spire libraries and citadel armouries for anything magical, and used Sky magic to strip the Night aspect from the Tilphussian Reach. Sadogua, the Whisper Gallery, the Azoth and Phaleron each offered to rebuild it, all needing a Conclave declaration of acceptance. Phaleron's offer was accepted, and the arcane projection to entreat the guardian Phoebus Al-Pulpi was delivered in Summer 388YE. Umarth's prophecy about retaking Elos also gave the Synod an opportunity to consecrate the docks with true liao, binding Wintermark and Urizen.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their incursions are cited as usually requiring major Senate repairs, and their past attack on Canterspire is recalled as when Phaleron first intervened.
n.Grendel: Grendel invaders were driven from Redoubt, but they carried off arcane texts and magical equipment and used Sky magic to wreck the Tilphussian Reach's Night aspect, for purposes that remained unknown.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the in-character scene features Myfanwy and Gavyn of the Black Thorns arguing on the ruined Elos docks.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs are noted as an exception to Grendel naval dominance, and the Azoth's cauldron would grow marsh flowers last seen in Madruga.
n.Urizen: Urizen's spires recovered Redoubt but lost arcane texts and the Tower of Light and Shadow. Its magicians weighed four eternal offers to restore the regio, and the Conclave chose Phaleron's guardian, which would fall under the Emissary to the Celestial Library rather than the Penumbral Watcher.
n.Wintermark: Umarth "Winter's Flame" Kannask and the Fist of the Mountains were credited with saving Elos, and Umarth's prophecy about the banner raised at the docks opened a chance for the Synod to consecrate the site and tie Wintermark and Urizen together.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel sought to reaffirm their naval stranglehold on the bay, and Phaleron's guardian would remain until the last Spine-Cracker navy is sunk in the Catazar.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Azoth's proposed cauldron would grow marsh flowers last seen in Madruga.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named directly; the page concerns events in neighbouring Redoubt.
t.Redoubt: Freed from the Grendel, Redoubt found its spire libraries and citadel armouries stripped of magic but little other damage, leaving Elos ready for possible dock expansion and the consecration of the site where Umarth's banner was raised.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Gavyn of the Black Thorns hails from Therunin and jokes that nothing that swims there is fit to eat.

r.Redoubt/Naris: The Tilphussian Reach in Naris lost its tower and nearly all its Night aspect. With Phaleron's offer accepted, the regio would be aligned to the Celestial Library and guarded by Phoebus Al-Pulpi, making Naris harder to conquer.

Forging links.d: The House of the People gave twenty wains of white granite and forty doses of liao, plus sevensalve for Ambassador Accalon, unloaded at Oran. Sumaah volunteers in Feroz offered to halve the labour cost of one single-season commission there, if a Senate motion asks for their help. A Winter Liberty Pact meeting chaired by Axos dissolved into confusion over tie-breaks, and only three of seven points stood. Judging the Pact's anti-slavery aims largely won, Oxtitocszin proposed ending regular meetings and leaving Pact business to ambassadors. Sumaah also agreed to one Senate-arranged appraisal of magical cooperation, available until the end of the Spring Equinox 388YE.

n.Dawn: Five Dawnish captains, including Ser Raine de Sarroi and Sir Edmund de Verlaine, helped escort the Stone Fleet, and Jarrigk Silktongue of Dawn, as Voice of Liberty, faces Sumaah's proposal to end Liberty Pact meetings.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; its only link is holding part of Feroz, where the Sumaah aid was delivered.
n.Highguard: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard was to collect the aid package at Anvil for distribution to the Freeborn and had brokered the magical cooperation offer, while Highborn captains including Raoul, Samuel and Tyden sailed in the escort.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Protectorate Kardak is listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Alim Longstride, Llandun Waystone and Derwyn are listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn supplied most of the escort captains and are the intended recipients of the granite, the liao meant to fortify their Pride, and the Sumaah volunteers' help rebuilding Feroz.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: around ten League captains, including Giovanni von Temeschwar and Albrecht von Holberg, are listed among the Stone Fleet's escort.
n.Urizen: Xanthippe, Grandmaster of the Celestial Arch, originated the magical cooperation proposal, though Sumaah refused any work on astronomancy as heretical; Xanthippe and Cerewyn, Magnus of Starfall, also sailed in the escort.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Triska Markova, Sokol Bradach Uzbek and Rudolfs Kafka are listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Beornwulf Redwaldsson is listed among the captains who escorted the Stone Fleet.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Asavean agents threatened to intercept the Sumaah convoy bound for the Bay of Catazar, prompting the Imperial escort.
t.Feroz: Feroz received twenty wains of white granite and Sumaah volunteers who are repairing homes and offering medicines, and they would halve the labour cost of one single-season Senate commission raised there this season.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The Stone Fleet sailed along the Fontargenta coast to Oran, where it unloaded the white granite donated for rebuilding.

Gossamer threads.d: The Wings of Kobol navy defeated the Wreckers in the Cazar Straits, and the Dukes refused to cede the islands. They planned to take Free Landing after the Spring Equinox and invited Freeborn fleets to join, offering loot and, with 4000 military strength, access to Atalaya's relics. A hakima, Indira 'Stormdancer' i Guerra, proposed an ilium-enhanced curse on Madruga to wreck the assault at heavy local cost. Suranni troops attacked Reinos, and Duke Guiscard of Arbonne sought supply passage through Segura for mithril. Four conjunctions involved the Hand of Dumon and a fleeing Lasambrian warband.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are recalled as earlier conquerors of the Cazar Straits, as holders of some lost corsair wealth, and as having once saved the Naguerro sept from destruction.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun homeland of Reinos came under Suranni attack, raising fears it might meet Kalino's fate while the rest of the Jotun look elsewhere. A fleeing Lasambrian warband carried intelligence on the invaders.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleets were invited to join the Suranni assault on Free Landing for loot and a chance to reclaim Atalaya's relics. A Freeborn hakima instead proposed a costly curse on Madruga to make the attack fail.
n.The League: A sect of the Hand of Dumon plotted to curse the Suranni embassy in Sarvos, and the Dukes suggested land around that embassy might be ceded to them as trade premises.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark historical researcher Marko Siwarsbairn was seized by the Hand of Dumon while returning through Arbonne, to be sacrificed unless rescued along with his research.

t.Bay of Catazar: Many Wrecker vessels fled the Bay of Catazar after their defeat, and the civil service found that Feroz cannot be cut off from the bay while the Bay of Oran stays in Imperial hands.
t.Feroz: The Suranni held the Cazar Straits and would not give them up. The Hand of Dumon moved to sacrifice the herd of Afar, and a Suranni invasion of Oranseri would isolate Feroz's ships.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: curse-warding designs by Richard of Holberg are cited as a precedent for a Suranni anti-curse temple.
t.Kalino: Called Arbonne by the Suranni, it remained plagued by Hand of Dumon curses and was the launch point for attacks on Feroz and Reinos. Its Duke sought ilium for a protective temple.
t.Madruga: The Suranni planned to take Free Landing, and a proposed ilium-enhanced curse to stop them would cost Madruga's fleets, farms, herb gardens and coastal settlements heavily.
t.Reinos: A significant Suranni force invaded from Arbonne after the Winter Solstice. Its progress is unknown because the Imperial spy network there had been decommissioned.
t.Sarvos: Hand of Dumon diabolists prepared to call down a curse on the Suranni embassy, and the Dukes suggested land around the embassy as possible trade premises.
t.Segura: The Dukes proposed a treaty letting Suranni supply lines pass through Segura in exchange for mithril for Kabalai Palace. A fleeing Lasambrian warband was also targeted there.
t.Shavronne: Mentioned in passing: Baron du Bestel of Shavronne wrote to the Champion of Ambition asking for the Lasambrian warband to be destroyed.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the ambassador's seat of Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Seized from the Children of Wrecks by two Suranni armies, the islands are claimed by the Confederacy. Trapped Freeborn are free to leave on Suranni ships.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oranseri's Bay of Oran keeps Feroz connected to the wider sea, and the Dukes might help bridge the Scorrero there. A Suranni invasion would isolate Feroz's ships.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: If the proposed curse were cast, work on the municipal docks funded by Gisli 'Provider' Baerson would halt, delaying completion to Spring 389YE.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Wings of Kobol planned to attack the Wreckers here after the Spring Equinox, with Freeborn fleets invited. A rival plan proposed devastating storms to turn the Suranni back.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: If the proposed curse were cast, work on the Well of Life would be delayed by three months.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Oran is described as stretching between Oranseri and Siroc Bayou.
r.Reinos/Chaveiro: Chaveiro's plains are speculated to be the first target of the Suranni invasion, though this rests only on the lie of the land.

Grace that comes with healing.d: With Ylenwe's Dawn Chorus aiding the work, the River Doubt was dammed, flooding much of Apstrus, and part of its flow was diverted to Icarion. Kirriemuir in Icarion gained a fizzing Day-regio spring, offering a Senate opportunity for a beauty spot that would encourage Yerende settlement. Ylenwe proposed the Harmonious Chimes edifice in Screed which, with music by Hieronymus Dowland, Lirielen Starsong and Kespoena Archsky, would quiet the Black Plateau for a year, though Pawdrig duSesna warned this could invite Grendel invasion. Ylenwe also offered to name a Cultivator of Solace, now illegal to accept, and sought to discuss a holistic manifesto with the Silver Chalice.

n.Dawn: Hieronymus Dowland of Dawn was asked to perform his perfect piece in the Hall of Worlds and was Ylenwe's first choice to be offered the role of Cultivator of Solace, though accepting it would now be illegal under the Synod's proscription.
n.Grendel: The Salt Lords Council, having lost entire armies when the Black Plateau exploded, are wary of invading Spiral while it rages, so quieting it could remove a deterrent against a Grendel invasion.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs ensured none of their kin's bones lie beneath the Apstrus reservoir and inscribed the names of their fallen at Solen's Doubt into the dam, and their senators would appoint the proposed Keeper of the Kirriemuir Campgrounds.
n.The League: Red Raven Holdings built the Dreaming Spire as a League gift to Urizen Spiralites, while Pawdrig of the duSesna Guild of Reckoners argued that the Black Plateau may be helping to keep Grendel armies away from Apulian.
n.Urizen: The texts of the drowned Solen's Doubt library were moved to the Dreaming Spire, the new Omphalos and heart of the Urizen nation, and Urizen's Lirielen Starsong and Kespoena Archsky were asked to perform the music needed to soothe the Black Plateau.

t.Mareave: Water diverted from the dammed Doubt is reducing Mareave's aridity, with Icarion fast becoming an oasis and a Day-regio spring rising at Kirriemuir.
t.Spiral: Spiral saw the Doubt dammed and the Dreaming Spire completed, and was offered a chance to quiet the Black Plateau for a year, at the possible risk of losing its deterrent effect on Grendel.

r.Mareave/Icarion: Icarion is thriving on the Lesser Doubt's waters, and the Senate may develop the Kirriemuir campgrounds into a beauty spot producing prismatic ink and giving the region the Yerende quality.
r.Spiral/Ankra: The Dreaming Spire now stands on Mount Cinnius in Ankra, housing the Omphalos of Urizen and the rescued Library of Solen's Doubt.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Much of Apstrus, including the Solen's Doubt battle site, now lies beneath a calm reservoir behind the Holbergian-designed dam, and the region gained the ruins and marsh qualities.
r.Spiral/Screed: Ylenwe proposed the Harmonious Chimes, thirteen mithril and ilium monoliths spiralling out across Screed from the Black Plateau, to lull it to quiescence for a year and open the way to a permanent solution.

Journeys end in lovers meeting.d: Freeborn from a Crucible parador planned to bring transformative rainbow water to the Brass Coast camp. Tasya of the Black Feathers invited named Varushkans to meet Irontooth, who intends to do something for Karsk. Marracossans from Trajadoz sought to renegotiate their treaty. Mendicant Garev, called to inquisition, was trapped in Kaela's regio near Syrene and needed rescuing. Armed Summer boggarts, heralds of the Azoth, a mysterious King Rat from Temeschwar and would-be cicisbeo were all heading for the League. Hahnmark stormcrows sought hosts for restless ghosts, and Kaisa the Sewn Tongue's sister sought answers about the Falconer cult. The Circle of Black Sand came to conclude a deal, and the rejected Tribunal of the Silver Flame sought out its Urizeni supporters.

n.Dawn: Mendicant Garev became lost in the regio near Syrene controlled by Kaela, a place Dawn's locals avoid because it saps the strength of all who enter.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as the foe the Red Wind Corsairs escaped and the enemy the Marracossans fought alongside the Empire.
n.Highguard: Highborn Mendicant Garev, called to inquisition by the Inquisitor of Prosperity, was stranded in a draining regio and needed rescue. He asked the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly to find him an advocate.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn from the Crucible parador came to the Brass Coast camp to celebrate with lineage-changing water. Marracossans also arrived there to meet their Sendito and the senator for Madruga about deepening their treaty.
n.The League: The League camp expected heralds of the Azoth offering transformative trials to League artisans, the sinister King Rat from Temeschwar and two aspiring cicisbeo from Spiral. Armed boggarts were also being herded from Spiral Castle towards Anvil.
n.Urizen: The Tribunal of the Silver Flame, whom the Urizen National Assembly had declared to be Urizen, planned to visit the Urizen camp. They wished to meet Callista of the Dark Shard and other supporters after the Conclave condemned their offer.
n.Varushka: Irontooth, pleased with Varushkan tribute, invited named Varushkans and representatives of two Karsk vales to a conjunction to discuss what Karsk needs. He also sent pointed messages to others who had courted him.
n.Wintermark: Stormcrows led by Grey Aleks brought Hahnmark's restless ghosts to the Tree of Names seeking willing hosts. Kiara Last-Lantern came to Sigehold Hall to learn about the Falconer cult that claimed her sister.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is noted as the site of Anvil, and Garev's earlier fall into a fissure near Casfall is recalled.
t.Hahnmark: The casting of Regrow the Land's Heart in Hahnmark uncovered the bones of the restless dead in war-scarred land, raising ghosts that could not be exorcised.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the Winter's Guest of Karov was warned by Irontooth not to intrude on the Charnel Lord's affairs.
t.Karsk: Irontooth intends to do something for the people of Karsk and invited two representatives each from the Vales of Utovshy and Yarizov to discuss what the territory needs.
t.Madruga: Freeborn from Madruga's Crucible brought their transformative fountain water to Anvil. Marracossans from Trajadoz sought the senator for Madruga to renegotiate their treaty with the Empire.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Irontooth questioned why a self-styled True Son of Karsk now bases his military unit in Ossium.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Kaisa the Sewn Tongue, the executed leader of the Falconer cult, is noted as coming from Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: An irritable yeofolk from Spiral Castle herded armed boggarts to Anvil, and two new League citizens from Spiral sought advice on becoming cicisbeo. The Silver Flame also called Spiral the heart of Urizen.
t.Temeschwar: A creature calling itself King Rat, a name tied to Temeschwar's rat plague and to strange deaths in the city, travelled south from Temeschwar towards Anvil.
t.Weirwater: Mendicant Garev was given poor directions near Syrene and is lying exhausted in Kaela's regio there, reachable by a Sentinel Gate conjunction on Saturday.

r.Casinea/Casfall: Mentioned in passing: Garev's fall into one of the fissures around Casfall last season, and his rescue, are recalled.
r.Madruga/Crucible: The Freeborn who keep the old parador fountain in Crucible, whose rainbow waters can grant naga, briar or draughir lineage, travelled to Anvil to celebrate the Red Wind Corsairs' victory.

Key of dreams.d: Cathan Canae agreed to a parley through her Thane of the Rimebound Shore but refused ever to renew the Fist of Black Ice. She demanded the ruined ritual text back and planned to reward the Phoenix Rising coven for raising her citadel in Hope's Rest. Azoth opened a Shadow Souk night market. Phaleron offered a pocket of its archives and lectors to channel writings of four lost cultures. Wise Rangara invited six Varushkan storytellers to hear her tales. Ptolemy of the City of Salt and Sail sought a preliminary parley with the Archmage of Autumn. Arhallogen declined to parley and offered boons for lifting interdictions or declaring enmities, two of which the Conclave took up.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's citadel stands in Hope's Rest in the Barrens, a territory held by Dawn, and she means to reward the coven that raised it.
n.Druj: Arhallogen cited the Empire's treatment of the Druj in Nesustak Forest as the reason she would make no offer about the Druj armies and septs being conquered. She also called the Rivers Run Red ritual she offered well known to the Druj.
n.Grendel: Arhallogen promised that if Ossegrahn were placed under enmity she would help the Empire against the Orcs of the Broken Shore, which would mean killing many Grendel. She warned that the Grendel themselves were also seeking a boon from Ossegrahn. The Conclave did place Ossegrahn under enmity.

t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen's herald appeared at Spiral Castle, and the Senator for Spiral, Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, might be brought to the Cathan Canae parley.
t.The Barrens: Cathan Canae acknowledged that her citadel had been called forth in Hope's Rest in the Barrens. She planned to give the Phoenix Rising coven a personal gift for that work.

r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Queen of Ice and Darkness meant to reward the Phoenix Rising coven for raising her citadel in Hope's Rest. Her herald would imbue an unworked set of mage armour, brought by the coven, with a shard of her power.

Lay the foundations.d: The judgement passed 750-0 with a greater majority. Just over two years in, slightly more than two-thirds of the thousand wains has been contributed, and a little over 281 wains of white granite are still needed. Popular support added four ranks to the Cinderpath Exchange for at least a year. The Senate could approve seven mithril bells in place of 49 wains of white granite. The City of Gold and Lead will offer to buy one Highborn commission each season. Congregations can preach the Second Age of Virtue to cut labour costs. The Custodes Clavium offer to empower the Highborn Speaker if the work is finished by Spring 389YE. The Assembly must also choose which Virtue titles receive offices first.

n.Highguard: Highguard has made the Grand Inspiration its highest calling, leaving fewer chances to attend to other matters. Its citizens are pooling resources to buy white granite, and its Assembly is invited to direct how the holy site's interiors and offices will be used.

t.Bastion: The vast, unfinished Grand Inspiration with its seven towers is rising in Bastion and already awes visitors. Volunteers inspired by the Second Age preaching may come to help build it, and Bastion's senator gets the City of Gold and Lead's commission offer in Autumn 388YE.
t.Casinea: Casinea's senator will receive the City of Gold and Lead's chit in Winter 388YE, allowing a single Casinean structure to be offered for sale to the City.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis's senator goes first: this summit they can use Ephisis' Scale to put one Necropolis commission up for sale to the City of Gold and Lead. Any deal still needs Senate approval at the next summit.
t.Reikos: Reikos's senator will receive the City of Gold and Lead's chit in Summer 388YE, allowing one structure in Reikos to be put up for sale to fund the Grand Inspiration.

Lean and athirst.d: Championed by Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh, with Ambassador Kindra Surefoot raising the matter with Otkodov, more than seventy Varushkan units joined Thule warlocks and hunters to execute trudniki wherever found. Draughir in Karsk and Ossium were questioned, often via insight ceremonies, though without violence. The unpopular Ketsov funded a bonus to units protecting the vales and hope for national recognition. Hunters recovered forest materials and a strength-giving concoction, elder's gift, which wise ones asked the Apothecaries Guild to assess and report on in the Senate; the Constitutional Court confirmed the Guild could share such findings. The waning warding power of Varushka's roads was mysteriously restored, and Sentinel Gate conjunctions revealed troubled wagon raiders in Drownbark Forest and Karsk.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish questing-knights are credited, alongside the schlacta, with helping keep monsters at bay while Varushka's road wards weakened.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov of Ossium are resented for having suffered less under the Druj yoke than their neighbours.
n.Thule: On the instruction of the Dragons of Otkodov, the Claws of the Dragon and Thule hunters worked with Varushka, leading the hunt in Krevsaty, the Bonewood and the Webwood and supporting Imperial efforts elsewhere. The Thule reportedly have no use for elder's gift and might sell it to the Speaker to the Leshun.
n.Varushka: Varushkan schlacta, wagon raiders and wardens wiped out the trudniki and gained loot, but draughir and reclusive citizens in Karsk and Ossium suffered suspicion and lost production. The roads' protective power was restored and the Ketsov's funding boosted units protecting the vales.

t.Karsk: Karsk was swept for trudniki dens and disguised face-peelers, leaving its draughir under suspicion. A sickened band of wagon raiders, the Gregadze, shunned by a local outpost, await treatment from the Apothecaries Guild.
t.Ossium: Ossium was a main focus of the hunt, with its draughir investigated and its Ketsov family funding the defence of the vales. Wagon raiders who pressed into Drownbark Forest have since been bewitched.
t.Otkodov: The Dragons of Otkodov ordered the Claws of the Dragon to help Varushka, and human vales in regions ceded to Otkodov were searched for trudniki hiding among them.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule Claws of the Dragon took the lead in hunting trudniki in Krevsaty, including among the human vales left under orc rule.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Claws of the Dragon led the search for face-peeler nests and hidden trudniki in the Bonewood.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Wagon raiders from Orieb who punted into the flooding Drownbark marshes seeking trudniki plunder have fallen prey to some spiritual force, and the Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market must investigate their stranded camp.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Webwood held the largest known trudniki den, making Thule cooperation vital; the Claws of the Dragon led operations there.

Monarchs and outcasts.d: The Prince with a Thousand Foes was outraged that his gifted Protector's Stone was destroyed with Words of Ending. Llofir raised his offer for herbs to fund a Navarr army against the vallorn. The Summer regents granted boons to Dawn's Knight-Protectors. Ephisis offered to buy the Quicksilver's Flame, auctioned a final vault and proposed Counting Houses in Kallavesa, the Barrens or Hercynia. Khobel Tavah held Eilian Sweetwater safe with dangerous 'jetsam'. Sorin, Agramant, Sinokenon, Kimus, Janon, Sadogua and Lashonar also made overtures or complaints. Outcome: the Navarr gave 750 marrowort for 15 mithril towards their fourth army, the Quicksilver's Flame was not sold, and the Counting House proposals were requested.

n.Dawn: Dawn's victory in the Drottningbjotha earned each Knight-Protector a boon from a Summer regent, with Meraud and Adamant's favours granted this season and the others awaiting new elections, while the Barrens was named a Counting House candidate.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Redoubt in 387YE is the reason Eilian Sweetwater fled into the Cave of the Drowned, and Sinokenon once warned Tsark of a Grendel raid.
n.Highguard: Elodian of Eleonaris sought out Lucifer, the new General of the Valiant Pegasus and Sychar of Ebon's Hall to learn why Highborn soldiers treated her warband strangely in Mitwold, while Highguard's chapter houses showed little interest in Janon's cursed 'blessings'.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sorin praised the Unshackled, Karrak, Stormsteel Skorr and new Archmage of Winter Bloodcrow Arora, still seeking a declaration giving him the tomb in Eoradal, and summoned Umarth Kannask, Odd Twiceborn and Towlen Nighthaven to have their weaknesses enumerated.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe was born in Mournwold while it was under Jotun rule, clouding whether he ever swore oaths to the Marches.
n.Navarr: Llofir offered 20 mithril for 1,000 same-type herbs to equip an army sworn to destroy the vallorn; the Navarr gave 750 marrowort via Avery Farkas and received 15 mithril towards their fourth army, and Hercynia was named a Counting House candidate.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Ephisis passed over the thriving League cities as Counting House sites, and Lashonar urged magistrates to begin their theft inquiry with the League's Guild of Ash and Embers.
n.The Marches: The Prince with a Thousand Foes dared anyone to cast Forge the Wooden Fastness in Alderly again, and the Lictors found no evidence that Stephen of Sarcombe was ever oathbound to the Marches, though a Reckoner would meet the Sun Chamber.
n.Urizen: Ephisis offered to buy the Quicksilver's Flame in Morrow (the sale did not happen), Kimus summoned Volidus over a Delving coven studying Cold Sun, and Leviathan withdrew its interest in Clytemnestra's Sword of Damakhan.
n.Varushka: Agramant offered any Varushkan who sent a bloodied handprint with Tribute to the Thrice Cursed Court a twig talisman to contact him, and Sadogua blamed a Varushkan named Vaclav for the Synod judgement calling him Dumon the Liar.
n.Wintermark: Callidus sent secretaries to empower Wintermark's maggots, the enmity-bound Whisper Gallery illegally offered crystal fire for Steinr poetry, and Kallavesa was named the top Counting House candidate.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Meraud proposed loosing three giants into Astolat's forests to test the yeofolk, an idea abandoned when the Summer regents settled on individual boons.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia was the third of three territories Ephisis judged would benefit from a Counting House boosting trade and taxation, and the Conclave accepted the offer to draw up proposals.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.
t.Kallavesa: Ephisis judged Kallavesa the territory that would benefit most from a Counting House, which would need at least thirty wains and be ceded to the City; the Conclave accepted the offer to draw up proposals.
t.Mareave: Sorin still sought a declaration granting him the contents of the tomb of Alicia-who-knew-the-path in Mareave, a bargain he felt events there this season made more useful.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Elodian's hammersmiths fought alongside the Green Shields and the Valiant Pegasus in Mitwold, where she felt the Highborn treated her strangely.
t.Morrow: Ephisis offered 80 wains of white granite and 240 crowns to dismantle and remove the Quicksilver's Flame in Morrow, but the fortification was not sold.
t.Mournwold: Stephen of Sarcombe was born in Mournwold under Jotun rule, complicating the Lictors' search for oaths to the Marches, and Shacklebreaker's anger threatened Forge the Wooden Fastness in Alderly.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named; its only connection is Agramant's boon to Varushkan citizens generally.
t.Redoubt: Eilian Sweetwater vanished at Nikephoros during the Grendel invasion of Redoubt and is held by Khobel Tavah in the Cave of the Drowned, while a Delving coven worked with Kimus to study Cold Sun at Terminus Sol.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is not named on the page; at most it is covered by the general note that Ephisis excluded war-torn territories from its Counting House plans.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar was listed among the thriving League cities Ephisis passed over for a Counting House.
t.The Barrens: Ephisis named the Barrens the second of three territories that would benefit from a Counting House where trade is scarce, and the Conclave accepted the offer to draw up proposals.

r.Mareave/Eoradal: Sorin hoped the new Archmage of Winter would ease a declaration offering him the contents of the tomb of Alicia-who-knew-the-path in Eoradal in exchange for a great boon.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The Prince with a Thousand Foes dared the Empire to cast Forge the Wooden Fastness in Alderly again, implying the ritual there may be unreliable until he is placated.

Old blue banners dancing.d: Most Jotun armies left Bregasland for Hordalant, leaving the Howling Night, Iron Host, Shield of the Mountain, Southern Bear and the Bear Who Swims to hold it. The Strong Reeds and Bounders were joined by the Narwhal's Spear, Autumn Hammers, Fire of the South and Burning Falcon. Nearly three thousand Imperial soldiers and at least two thousand Jotun died. Unexplained magic raised a woodland on the Gravenmarch–Rushes border, and landskeepers fear its link to Graven Rock. A battle opportunity followed in the Grey Fens: stop ghodi Sunne Astar taking the Ullsmere Rock to Hordalant, banish the Grey Walker shades, and possibly rescue Friar Bloughton of House Brawness.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the only link is a note that the Fire of the South fought alongside the Knights of Glory in Sarangrave the previous Summer.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: uneasy landskeepers looked south-east towards Casinea and Anvil as they muttered about the strange forest.
n.Jotun: The Jotun pulled most of their forces back to Hordalant and lost Gravenmarch, with at least two thousand dead, but five armies still held the rest of Bregasland. Ghodi Sunne Astar sought the Ullsmere Rock to strengthen the Howling Night.
n.The Marches: Led by the Strong Reeds and Bounders, the Marchers reclaimed Gravenmarch as a beachhead in Bregasland, while the Drakes went to defend Mitwold. They were also offered a chance to reopen talks with the once-rebellious House Brawness.
n.Wintermark: The Narwhal's Spear marched south from Skallahn and fought at the right hand of the final Imperial advance. Its general was given a chance to seize Jotun supplies bound for the Southern Bear, while the Bloodcloaks fell back to Hahnmark.

t.Bregasland: Six Imperial armies fought five Jotun armies here and liberated Gravenmarch at a cost of thousands of lives. The rest of the territory, including the Rushes and the Grey Fens, remained contested.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: landskeepers cast baleful glances towards Casinea and Anvil after the forest appeared.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the Bloodcloaks fell back to Hahnmark from Bregasland.
t.Hordalant: Most of the Jotun armies withdrawn from Bregasland raced west to Hordalant, and ghodi Sunne Astar planned to drag the Ullsmere Rock there.
t.Mitwold: Four Jotun armies returned from Mitwold to Bregasland while Lasambrian forces held the territory. The Drakes answered the call to defend it against the unexpected invasion.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the warband of Yantan Tethrason of Reinos, a former Lasambrian goatherd, fought for the Jotun in the south of Bregasland.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South last fought alongside the Knights of Glory in Sarangrave during the Summer.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies that had been attacking in Skallahn moved south to Bregasland, the Burning Falcon having been denied a true battle there.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch was liberated after brutal fighting beneath Graven Rock, which roared during the final battle. A forest now stands in its west, grown from the fallen.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Jotun warriors dragged away the Ullsmere Rock at Drayham Mere, releasing the Grey Walker shades. The region will become haunted unless the stone is restored.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: House Brawness, still resentful and rebellious, keeps to its farm here. Rescuing its friar could open talks to resolve the region's rebellious spirit.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders' general named the Ottermire as a target, and Helma Skutasdóttir's warband was rooting out Bregas rebels in Ottery.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The Empire pushed the Jotun back into the Rushes and made some headway there, and a supernatural woodland rose overnight along its border with Gravenmarch.
r.Hordalant/Vallorberg: Ghodi Sunne Astar intended to place the Ullsmere Rock in Vallorberg's kirkja sacred to Ulven, believing it would raise the fighting spirit of the Howling Night.

On the road ahead.d: Anduz, built from the ruins of a pre-Imperial city and sacked by the Lasambrians in 363YE, faced four options. The Brazen Propylaeum would make it the City of Adventure and inspire Trailblazers. The Market of a Thousand Sails would make it the City of Deals with Hawkers. The Burning Agora, a torchlit space for debate proposed partly as a counterweight to fears of Highborn orthodoxy, would make it the City of Passions with Firebrands. Dust, Glass and Flame would combine all three with an ilium-enchanted fountain, making it the City of Wonders, but it needed a foundational artwork and a far larger cost. If nothing was built, Anduzjasse would gain the ruins quality as the City of Stones.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: their attempt to catch the Red Wind Corsairs is said to have been countered by Freeborn cunning.
n.Highguard: Some Freeborn, especially the Riquezans, feared the Highborn might use the Grand Inspiration of the Way to push a rigidly orthodox doctrine, and the Burning Agora was proposed as a counterweight to that.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun forces are noted as still pressing into the Marches.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn National Assembly passed the mandates for the Cities of Deals, Passions and Wonders, which could create the Hawker and Firebrand archetypes once their edifices are built. Work then began on the costly Dust, Glass and Flame project to remake Anduz.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Segura is described as almost as far from Bastion as one can get and still be in the Empire, making it a fitting haven for free debate.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni are noted to have claimed the Cazar Straits in Feroz, while showing no sign of attacking the mainland.
t.Segura: Segura, already enjoying prosperity from the Zemress Islanders and the restored Towers of Anduz, saw its chief city set on course to become the City of Wonders, with construction beginning in Summer 388YE.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni are said to have laid claim to the Cazar Straits.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Anduzjasse was offered edifices that would fix its city's fate, and building began on Dust, Glass and Flame, combining the Propylaeum, the Market of a Thousand Sails, the Burning Agora and an enchanted Fountain of Wonders. If work stalls for a year, the region instead gains the ruins quality.

Other monstrous geographies.d: Under the Rivers of Life curse, the Eastern Sky, Lions of Adelmar, Summer Storm, Citadel Guard and Quiet Step took Sephals and broke the Tower of the Skink's gate with a stone-and-mithril ram, capturing Thornfen. The Hidden Snake and Poison Crane fled to the Salt Flats, losing 500 more each, and the scattered garrison left Outlaw Druj across four regions. The Gryphon's Pride crushed Banded Snake and Thornwasp attacks on Nesustak. The Boyar's Hasta only partly thwarted the Tainted Basilisk, who loosed Béantal Dol on Nesustak and Bloodwater Marsh. A Senate motion will confirm the Axou claim to Thornfen, and the Drowned Man is now called the Drowned Shepherd.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Eastern Sky and Lions of Adelmar led the breach of the Tower of the Skink, while the Gryphon's Pride saved the Nesustak rebels and won their wary trust; the Strategos of Dawn must now rescue sept members from Druj ghosts at Dahis.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Sephals, the Tower of the Skink and their last hold on the Sarangrave, their Hidden Snake and Poison Crane fleeing to the Salt Flats, though the Tainted Basilisk spitefully unleashed the vallorn of Béantal Dol.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; Bregasland, which they held, appears only in a comparison between its Otterway and the Tail of the Skink.
n.Navarr: The Navarr of the Quiet Step hunted Druj across the marshes, struck the Druj flanking force at the Tower, and with freed Great Forest Orcs built the weirwood frame for the ram that broke its gate.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is listed among the places where the Druj have tried to make examples of those who escaped them.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard helped take the Tower, which gives Urizen control of Thornfen; the Urizen assembly may veto the coming motion ceding it to the Axou, and Urizeni seers captured in Bloodwater Marsh await rescue.
n.Varushka: Varushka's Boyar's Hasta scouted for every Imperial army and ambushed the Tainted Basilisk's ghulai, limiting the vallorn's release to two regions; its general must now clear ghosts that took Hasta scouts near Béantal Dol.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step marched from Astolat into the Sarangrave.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the raised Tail of the Skink causeway is likened to Otterway in Bregasland.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Béantal Dol is described as a vallorn with the full power of Brocéliande packed into a single region.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: named as one place where the Druj have sought to punish those who threw off their yoke.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj have attacked escaped slaves, and toasted by the Hasta's general for Varushkans slaying peelers there.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The battered Hidden Snake and Poison Crane fled to the Salt Flats, a temporary refuge where desertion is expected, after supplies smuggled from there had armed the attack on Nesustak.
t.Sarangrave: The Empire now holds all of the Sarangrave save Nesustak Forest and Bendol, but the unleashed vallorn, floods, a surge of vermin and Outlaw Druj in four regions blight its conquest.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky, Gryphon's Pride and Citadel Guard marched out of Semmerholm to join the campaign.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the relieving armies passed through the Barrens, which are also recalled as a place where the Druj punished their former slaves.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: recalled as the place where the Tainted Basilisk have previously shown themselves willing to unleash a vallorn.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The Tainted Basilisk breached the Terunael warding stones around Béantal Dol, freeing the vallorn; the remaining stones will be destroyed by the Summer Solstice, leaving it a potent but ordinary vallorn.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: The vallorn advances into Bloodwater Marsh at strength 30,000, and an equinox opportunity at Mantifent's Bier offers a chance to ward its stones, break the Bilious Breath and rescue captured Urizeni seers.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The fleeing Druj armies crossed north through Kroll to the Salt Flats, and the region now suffers from Outlaw Druj.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The rebels repelled Banded Snake and Thornwasp attackers with the Gryphon's Pride's help, but now face the vallorn at strength 30,000, with an equinox opportunity at the Feverbank Trees to ward the stones.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Sephals and the Tower of the Skink fell and Thornfen is now Imperial, though flooded and plagued by Outlaw Druj, with a Senate motion due to confirm the Axou claim to it.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The Gryphon's Pride camped in the western Turan Flats to guard Nesustak; the region now has Outlaw Druj, and Druj ghosts menace the Bloodwater Spears near the village of Dahis.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Four Great Forest Orcs freed from Whisperwood's weirwood grove helped build the ram's frame, but the region now suffers from Outlaw Druj.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies passed swiftly through the Bleaks, watched silently by the Karass.

Our elaborate plans.d: The magic in Apulian grew in 'vorticity': engaging things felt closer, rainbow cats warred with songbirds, and the thrones and personae began reshaping businesses and performances. Sung became less agitated but more reclusive. The League National Assembly was due to appoint the Map to the City Below, who could claim 37 crystal fire to recruit captains. A scouting venture, Map the City Below, was open to League, Urizen and Dawnish units, succeeding with 3000 strength despite unknown resistance. The duSesna Guild, whose prince Teodore had vanished after accusing Sung, offered a rival venture, Rescue the Missing Prince. Units assigned to it subtracted from the mapping effort, and the guild urged the Assembly to condemn Sung.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units were not formally invited but could join the Map the City Below venture if they found the quixotic adventure glorious enough, earning crystal fire and a rainbow feather.
n.The League: League citizens bore the brunt of Apulian's strange magic and its benefits. Their National Assembly faced appointing the Map to the City Below and answering the duSesna Guild's demand to condemn Sung, while League units were invited to map the city.
n.Urizen: Urizeni architects helped build the Chamber of Euphony and Urizeni scholars studied the city's magic. Urizen military units were invited to help map the sewers their forebears originally built.

t.Spiral: Apulian, Spiral's City Below, saw intensifying night magic. Resident night magicians gained ritual strength, and two rival scouting ventures in the city's tangled sewers were set against each other.

r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: the Greater Doubt, flowing more strongly from Apstrus since the dam's construction, feeds into Apulian's sewers.

Petals in the snow.d: The Kraft Brothers grow vlinderbloem in Hahnmark to brew the narcotic viezesmaak, while the rival Zuredruiven vintners have learned to cultivate draaikolkbloem at scale. Hahnmark's farm owners were to vote at the Tree of Names at the Spring Equinox on whether to keep growing vlinderbloem or end the Kraft deal. The Senate could commission the Zuredruiven Benefice in Kalpamark, raising herb garden investment and creating a Zuredruiven Cultivator title to trade draaikolkbloem for Woven Fortune, but this would drive the Kraft Brothers out. Alternatively, both partnerships could be ended amicably. Herb garden owners were also secretly offered draaikolkbloem in place of some herbs, but if more than 20 accepted, the Kraft Brothers would withdraw.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: rumour holds that Astolat's wines are finer than the Zuredruiven vintages.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Seguran vintages are said to compare favourably with the Zuredruiven wines.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a dubious bottle passed off as a genuine 312YE Sarvosi vintage features in the story, and Sarvos's wines are said to outclass the Zuredruiven ones.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's people had to decide between two rival Sarcophan partnerships, through a farmers' vote, a possible new Wintermark national title of Zuredruiven Cultivator, and a quiet offer to herb garden owners.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat's wines are cited as finer than those of the Zuredruiven vineyards.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's farmers and herb gardeners faced a choice between keeping vlinderbloem production for the Kraft Brothers, switching to the Zuredruiven vintners' draaikolkbloem, or ending both deals, with the risk that a mixed decision would drive both away.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a supposed Sarvosi vintage of 312YE appears in the story, and Sarvos wines are said to surpass the Zuredruiven vintages.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Seguran vintages are rumoured to be finer than the Zuredruiven wines.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: Kalpamark was the proposed site of the Zuredruiven Benefice, a great work that would raise herb garden investment, produce draaikolkbloem, or Imperial roseweald if the deal failed, at the cost of the Kraft Brothers' departure.

Push for victory.d: Vesna praised Navarr for privately funding its third army and commended several heroes. A Freeborn corsair, Aracely, proposed a raid on Leen through the Salt Flats smugglers' cove, which would expose the cove to destruction. The raid was an overwhelming success, freeing thousands of slaves. The Barossa School offered to make one army fast for ten wains of mithril. A Sand Fisher offer to approach a sept under Druj rule went unused. Dawn, the Imperial Orcs and Wintermark could enact mandates to raise military units. Highguard's benefactors offered to fund any commission. Further offers covered weirwood for the Breadbasket, Urizen mana sites (not enacted), a weirwood-built Navarr army, Delev mithril for the Throne, and a Rahvin attack on the Karass.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly could enact a mandate letting Dawnish citizens convert farms, mines, forests and similar holdings into military units of the same level in the same territory for a season.
n.Druj: Vesna declared the Druj a dying regime. Freeborn raiders struck Leen and freed thousands of their slaves, and the Rahvin sought leave to destroy the Karass, whom they call Druj servants.
n.Highguard: Inspired by the Throne, the Highborn Council of Benefactors agreed to direct its twelve wains a season to any commission, rather than only civilian works such as the Grand Inspiration of the Way.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly could enact a mandate encouraging the Unshackled to turn their holdings into military units of the same level, supporting the war on the Druj.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Vesna warned that the Jotun will see the Empire fight for what is its own from Bregasland to Sermersuaq to Tassato.
n.Navarr: Vesna praised Navarr for funding its third army without public money or bourse seats; that army finishes mustering at the Autumn Equinox 388YE. A further army could be raised with Great Forest Orc help, using weirwood in place of mithril, and Navarr supply will fall if no new army begins by Autumn 389YE.
n.The League: The League's third army in Tassato was funded two seasons early as Vesna's 'hand in the West'. The Barossa School offered to make an army fast, and the League Assembly could direct the Sand Fishers to approach a Druj-ruled sept, though that judgement was withdrawn.
n.The Marches: Alders of Wayford secured ten wains of weirwood for expanding the Marcher Breadbasket into the Mournwold, paid for by Keeper Orson BogMyrtle. Alders of Hay offered ten more for 30 thrones, and Vesna named the Marches among the nations that could raise more armies.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly faced two competing mandates to cut the cost of upgrading mana sites, one adding a contest between territories, but neither was enacted.
n.Varushka: A Delev consortium offered to sell the Throne up to forty wains of mithril a season, starting at three thrones a wain, to raise armies. Varushkans celebrated Vesna, even comparing him flatteringly with Empress Varkula.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly could enact a mandate letting citizens convert holdings into military units of the same level. Vesna also commended Ematius Ankarien for his years as Archmage of Winter.

t.Bastion: The Grand Inspiration of the Way under construction in Bastion could lose its twelve wains a season of Highborn funding if the Council of Benefactors redirected it to another commission.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Vesna named Bregasland among the western lands the Empire will fight to reclaim from the Jotun.
t.Hercynia: Navarr's third army was nearly mustered in Hercynia, with its general due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Hercynia was also a possible site for a new Navarr army built with weirwood.
t.Holberg: Three Hands wrote to Holberg's senator offering to have the Sand Fishers approach a sept under Druj rule. He warned that failure could harm the Empire's relations with Holberg's orcs, and no such approach was made.
t.Karov: Delev merchants, having completed the wards on the Little Boyar's Welcome, offered mithril from their vales and outposts to the Throne for raising armies, rather than selling it to the Commonwealth.
t.Miaren: Miaren was one of two possible sites for a new Navarr army built with weirwood, though such an army could not be combined with the Miaren opportunity to raise an army of vates.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold is not named directly; its relevance lies in the Marcher Breadbasket, whose expansion into the Mournwold was being supplied with weirwood through the alders of Wayford and Hay.
t.Mournwold: Ten wains of weirwood were set aside for expanding the Marcher Breadbasket into the Mournwold, and ten more were offered for 30 thrones if bought by the Summer Solstice.
t.Redoubt: Adelmar the Lion's Academy of Arms in Redoubt inspired a Urizen mandate for a contest between territories over mana investment, but it was not enacted.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The hidden Imperial smugglers' cove here was used to launch the Freeborn raid on Leen. The price of the raid was its exposure and destruction by the Druj after the corsairs evacuated it.
t.Sarangrave: Vesna declared the Empire on the verge of completing its conquest of the Sarangrave, with thoughts already turning to settling and building up the lands won there.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Vesna named Sermersuaq among the western lands the Empire will fight for against the Jotun.
t.Tassato: The third League army was mustering in Tassato, and the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy there offered to make any one army except the Argent Sword fast, for ten wains of mithril.
t.The Barrens: The Rahvin sought a chance to wipe out the Karass, whom they call Druj traitors in the Barrens, if the Empire declared war on that sept or ceded the Bleaks to it. The Barrens slave rebellion was also cited as the reason Druj-ruled septs distrust the Empire.
t.Therunin: Vesna commended the heroes who stopped the riling of the vallorn in Eastring. The Great Forest Orcs, who once offered to support an army in Therunin, renewed their pledge to help raise a Navarr army.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Throne's words reached the Misericorde Market, where the Sand Fishers resolved to try to persuade a Druj-ruled sept to trust the Empire, despite Three Hands' fears.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: Adelmar the Lion's Academy of Arms in the mountains of Siluri, now a place of pilgrimage, inspired Urizen's second, unenacted mandate.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Leen Rarckan: Freeborn corsairs raided Leen Rarckan with overwhelming success, freeing thousands of slaves, many of whom had never been Imperial citizens.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Rahvin army was still being raised in Bitter Strand, and some of its eager recruits offered to attack the Karass under General Utmar.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Karass of the Bleaks faced possible annihilation by the Rahvin if, during this one season, the Empire declared war on them or the Senate ceded the Bleaks to them.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Imperial heroes prevented the riling of the vallorn in Eastring, and Vesna commended the Vallornguard and Ser Rhydian de Rondell for leading and funding the skirmish.

Ripple of echoes.d: Llofir-empowered Regrow the Land's Heart erased Freya's Garden and the Tower of the Scorpion and filled Ossium and Hahnmark with marrowort. This offered sinecures and a time-limited great work. The Wise Flower Chapter offered to fund a Spring herb-garden ritual. A darkness linked to the Night Below unsettled Volodmartz and Miekarova, where mine owners were offered Blackdamp's aid or the chance to oppose it. Magistrates found Starwood Roots Steading's cannibals gone, with hints of Agramant behind them. Igraine's Regio cursed the Castle of Thorns. Suaq traders reported unexplained curse coins. The song 'Painted' kept spreading, prompting a proposed Nightingale Chorus Wayhouse in Astolat to rally Dawn against the vallorn.

n.Dawn: The Castle of Thorns suffered a hostile, frozen regio curse, and a proposed Astolat wayhouse would rally Dawnish nobles and yeofolk against the vallorn, with greater benefits if the Dawnish Assembly named that fight their Highest Calling.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: marrowort grew over the charnel pits and mass graves left in Ossium by the fight against the Druj.
n.Navarr: Navarr cannibals of Starwood Roots Steading escaped Hercynia's magistrates. The Navarr song 'Painted' kept spreading, offering Navarr a proposed Thorn Singer title and a spring surge of pride in their oaths.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Segura was named among the places where the echo of the Navarr song continued.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Spiral was named among the places where the echo of the Navarr song continued.
n.Varushka: Ossium bloomed with Llofir's growth and marrowort, offering a national Varushkan sinecure, while Volodmartz and Miekarova faced a creeping darkness tied to the Night Below and stories of the forgotten.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark was overgrown by Llofir's renewal, bringing marrowort bounties to several titles and possible sinecures, while Suaq traders grew uneasy at a rash of unexplained curse coins.

t.Astolat: The regio at the Castle of Thorns cursed the garden with unmelting snow and poisonous thorns, and the Senator of Astolat was made responsible. A wayhouse was proposed to boost units questing against the vallorn and raise taxes there.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the arcane projection that began the spreading song had been cast there the previous Autumn.
t.Hahnmark: Llofir's power reclaimed Freya's Garden and made the dead bloom with fungus, and marrowort covered the hillsides. Five titles gained extra marrowort, and a sinecure or great work could be commissioned there.
t.Hercynia: Magistrates climbed to Starwood Roots Steading to arrest its cannibals but found them fled, leaving only a note and a wicker box for the Senator of Hercynia.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Navarr with resources in Astolat would vote in the Miaren election if the Nightingale Chorus Wayhouse were built.
t.Miekarova: A sense of encroaching darkness weakened lightstones and gave stories of the forgotten new life. Mine owners could accept the Night Below's aid for extra deep stone or oppose it.
t.Ossium: The Tower of the Scorpion was overgrown and mass graves filled with marrowort, giving the Grieftender and every herb garden extra herbs and opening sinecure and great work opportunities.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where the echo of the Navarr song continued.
t.Semmerholm: Units there questing against the vallorn would gain from the proposed wayhouse only if the Dawnish Assembly named that fight its Highest Calling.
