t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where the echo of the Navarr song continued.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where the echo of the Navarr song continued.
t.Volodmartz: People feared the dark as lightstones dimmed and the Light Market was overwhelmed. A letter there offered mine owners Blackdamp's aid through Echo of Songs this season.
t.Weirwater: Units there questing against the vallorn would gain from the proposed wayhouse only if the Dawnish Assembly named that fight its Highest Calling.

r.Astolat/Grovesyard: The Nightingale Chorus Wayhouse at Brightway was proposed for expansion as the hub of a Navarri-Dawnish coalition against the vallorn.
r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: Near Valashal, a great work could be commissioned this season to capture Llofir's boon and give Hahnmark herb gardens three marrowort each season.
r.Miekarova/Perumaki: Mentioned in passing: a miner's tale of losing his brothers to a forgotten cavern began on the Perumaki path.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Tower of the Scorpion's site was reclaimed by fungal growth, where a Fellsting Grave sinecure, and possibly Freya's Legacy, could yield Llofir's donahorti.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The battlefields there could host a great work this season to give every Ossium herb garden three marrowort each season.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Mentioned in passing: an inn in Brez was where a miner told, then forgot, the tale of his lost brothers.

Saint of Bees.d: Bees fled or fell torpid when Cold Sun attacked, sensitive to shifts in mana, and the loss was slowly weakening plants, especially herb gardens. The priests of Zoloto in Skoremujac said the bees must be reassured the danger had passed. Two remedies were offered: a Highborn mandate sending a priest with 50 liao to spread Prosperity ceremonies, and a great work to build weirwood 'regal hives' in Malimorzi, available until the end of Winter 388YE. Unchecked, the decline would penalise Karov's herb gardens and farms, then its forests and businesses. At the Spring Equinox 388YE the mandate enacted by Ada of Balthazar's Vineyard was upheld, and Lepidean Librarian Hazelelponi called on Lepidean archivists to research Kvetmir.

n.Highguard: Highborn wayfarers and grey pilgrims went north to aid their Varushkan kin, and the Highborn Assembly upheld Ada of Balthazar's Vineyard's mandate to spread Kvetmir's inspiration and support Zoloto's work.
n.Varushka: Varushka's bees, cherished symbols of Prosperity in its folk tales, were disappearing from Karov and neighbouring territories, threatening its herb gardens, farms and wider prosperity. The upheld mandate was expected to halt the decline and slowly coax bees back over at least a year.

t.Karov: Karov was where the bee loss began after Cold Sun's attack. Unchecked, it would penalise its herb gardens and farms, and later its forests and businesses, while regal hives built there would restore its bees and boost its herb gardens.
t.Karsk: Deserted hives were reported in Kopevnost as the bee loss spread into Karsk, and regal hives could also be built in the territory to support its herb gardens.
t.Miekarova: Deserted hives and a dearth of bees were reported in Dupadealuri as the problem spread from Karov into Miekarova.
t.Reikos: Reikos's Highborn are no strangers to beekeeping, and if the regal hives in Karov were completed, Zoloto's bee tenders would come to help the Gardens of High Chalcis, giving Reikos herb gardens extra herbs for a year.
t.Volodmartz: As the bees vanished, plant health across Volodmartz began a subtle but worsening decline, with each generation of herbs in its gardens a little less potent than the last.

r.Karov/Duzekani: Duzekani, where the scions did the greatest damage, reported fewer bees, and its sunburned state was named as the root cause of the problem.
r.Karov/Kamienczka: Kamienczka was among the Karov regions where fewer bees were being encountered after Cold Sun's invasion.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: Malimorzi's folk reported fewer and fewer bees, and the region was chosen as the central site for the proposed regal hives, a great work offered until the end of Winter 388YE.
r.Karov/Skoremujac: Skoremujac reported fewer bees, and in its northern vale of Zoloto the devotees of Kvetmir Kvetmirovic, whose own bees were leaving, shared their beekeeping knowledge and hive designs with the Highborn.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Wieliczka was among the Karov regions where fewer bees were being encountered after Cold Sun's invasion.
r.Karsk/Kopevnost: Kopevnost reported deserted hives and few bees visiting the spring flowers as the decline spread beyond Karov.
r.Miekarova/Dupadealuri: Dupadealuri reported deserted hives and a marked lack of bees as the decline spread beyond Karov.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: Highborn arriving in Livardz to support its restoration found deserted hives and a shortage of bees there, prompting them to take up the bee problem.

Snap rope and pass foil.d: Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo's network was built mostly in northern Sermersuaq. It will scout Tsirku one region per season, beginning north of Suaq Fount, and needs far more strength than a normal spy network. Units from nations other than Wintermark and Varushka suffer a three-rank penalty. Army upkeep there is doubled, and in Autumn and Winter armies take casualties and scouting costs double. The Whisper Gallery will oppose the effort, Blood-on-the-Snow claims the land, and nobody returns from Sydanjaa. The opportunities include an Adventure in Tsirku venture, the Citadel of the Warm Hearth, new duties for the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, two Synod mandates, magical aid and a possible Senate statement recognising Wintermark's connection to Tsirku.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units may take the Adventure in Tsirku venture, but they suffer the same three-rank penalty that applies to scouting.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave, which the Druj hold, is named as a past challenge that Tsirku will dwarf.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, held by the Grendel, is named as a past challenge that Tsirku will dwarf.
n.Jotun: The Jotun border Tsirku through Tromsa and are expected to have opinions on Imperial interest there. Scouts at higher strength will report on any Jotun presence, though the Jotun have never conquered the wastes themselves.
n.Thule: The Thule border Tsirku to the east and are expected to react to Imperial interest. Scouts may uncover Thule presence and links to Otkodov, though the Thule have never mastered the wastes either.
n.Varushka: Alongside Wintermark, Varushkan units are best suited to the cold and suffer no rank penalty when supporting the Tsirku scouting network.
n.Wintermark: The Witan and the mystics of Ishal lead the effort. Wintermark gains the Adventure in Tsirku venture, the chance to build the Citadel of the Warm Hearth, two Synod mandates for its National Assembly, and a possible Senate recognition of its historic tie to Tsirku.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Regent of the Eternal Sea is recalled as having aided a dangerous Imperial foray into Brocéliande.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark's senator, Bron Dunwolf, had earlier proposed an appraisal of Tsirku exploration, which was withdrawn.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa are named among those whose custom of entering Sydanjaa predates the Empire.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory whose conquest challenges will pale beside those of Tsirku.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory whose conquest challenges will pale beside those of Tsirku.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: higher-strength scouting may reveal connections between Tsirku and Otkodov.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory whose conquest challenges will pale beside those of Tsirku.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: believed to border Tsirku, and its beasts are cited as a hint of what treasures Tsirku may hold.
t.Sermersuaq: The scouting lodges and supply stocks were built in northern Sermersuaq, and its roads would carry materials for the Citadel. A Synod mandate could divert the Smokehouse of Atalaq's output to supply the scouts instead of its farms.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: higher-strength scouting may reveal connections between Tsirku and Skallahn.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Tsirku is said to be larger than the Barrens, which is also named as a lesser conquest challenge.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Tromsa lies west of Tsirku, and scouts may report on links between the wastes and Tromsa.
t.Tsirku: The wastes became the target of a long, region-by-region scouting effort hampered by cold, doubled army upkeep, winter casualties, the Whisper Gallery, Blood-on-the-Snow and the deadly storm Sydanjaa.

r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: Urdur is described as lying to the east of Tsirku.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Scouting will begin in the region of Tsirku north of Suaq Fount, using the caching tradition of the hunters who range there.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Mentioned in passing: the supply-cache tradition of its hunters inspires the scouting method, and the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq prepares hunters for its dangers.

Sunrise over Livardz.d: Rebuilding needed two Senate commissions plus 20 thrones a season for a year, and a Triosk forestry whose wardens would clear wolves at the cost of a year of Iron Roads trade. The silent menace could be removed by walling up the Star Caverns under a Murupan Goose-herd and destroying the Sumisev Peegel with Wind of Mundane Silence. The ashen wind required a Wyrding Tower and laying the Shadow Fellowship's ghosts to rest. Solving two would lift the ruins; all three would bring the Security of Volodmartz. Most Highborn volunteers turned to the missing bees instead. The ghosts were dealt with at the Spring Equinox, the Sumisev Peegel was destroyed at Summer, and the Wyrding Tower was completed before Autumn.

n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is cited as proof that people can live almost anywhere.
n.Varushka: Varushkans faced the work of reclaiming Livardz. Their Assembly named Auntie Armand Mariyavich Remislav, who destroyed the Sumisev Peegel, and Borys Vardovich Straskovich, as Boyar of the Iron Roads, announced the Wyrding Tower.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Tower of the Eagle regio in Hahnmark is contrasted with the Sumisev Peegel.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: its Tower of the Eagle is noted as a regio that, unlike the Sumisev Peegel, seemed at risk of opening.
t.Karov: Karov, attacked by the Blade of Skies in 385YE, would have had its mines and forests each lose one level of investment if the Triosk forestry were commissioned.
t.Karsk: Karsk's mines and forests would each lose one level of investment for a year if the wardens were diverted from the Iron Roads to clear Livardz.
t.Miekarova: Its senator Vasilmir Radovanovna Esskivic seconded the motion, and its mines and forests would each lose one level of investment under the proposed forestry.
t.Ossium: Ossium's forests stood to lose two levels of investment for a year if the Triosk forestry drew the wardens away from the Iron Roads.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: cited as evidence that people can live almost anywhere.
t.Volodmartz: Clearing two of the three challenges would lift Livardz's ruins and raise treasury revenue by six thrones a season, and all three would grant a year of extra income across the territory. The ghosts, the Sumisev Peegel and the Wyrding Pond were all addressed.

r.Volodmartz/Livardz: Livardz was the focus of every proposal. The Shadow Fellowship's ghosts in the Sunless Vale were dealt with, the Sumisev Peegel was destroyed, and the Wyrding Tower was raised at the ash-choked Wyrding Pond.
r.Volodmartz/Murupa: Murupa holds the Star Caverns where the Shepherds of Ash vanished. A sinecure was proposed to wall them up behind wards and establish geese under a Murupan Goose-herd to watch over them.

The last assignment.d: The Celesti Lighthouse in Oranseri, Feroz, remains buildable largely unchanged. It would provide a rank one fortification, raise trading fleet investment, let Freeborn fleets guard Oranseri, remove its abandoned quality and restore a reworked Celesti Lighthouse Keeper. The Four Points fortification in Operus, Morrow, could be a rank two fortification, built in one year with a Urizen Assembly mandate. The original upgrade to Reumah's Rest in Necropolis was defunct. Mladen offered a cheap White Sails version, a rank three garrison with boats that can support Imperial navies, and an ambitious version with a warship flotilla able to intercept a barbarian navy. Only one can be commissioned. All are available until Spring 390YE.

n.Grendel: Grendel armadas, which often sail past Necropolis, could be forced into battle by the White Sails flotilla if the ambitious upgrade to Reumah's Rest were built. The southern coast forts were originally raised against Grendel invasion.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis could see Reumah's Rest raised to a rank three fortification, either as a cheap fort with boats or as an ambitious flotilla able to engage enemy navies off its coast.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn could gain the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz. It would let their fleets guard Oranseri and restore a Lighthouse Keeper chosen by Tally of the Votes, funded by willing donations from Freeborn captains.
n.Urizen: Urizen could see the Four Points fortification built in Morrow. A greater-majority mandate from the Urizen Assembly urging Loyal sentinels to join the garrison could halve its construction time.

t.Feroz: The opportunity to fortify the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz remains open until Spring 390YE. It would raise trading fleet investment in the territory by one and give it a garrison to patrol it.
t.Morrow: Morrow could gain a rank two fortification and garrison under the revived Four Points plan, which builds on the inspiration provided by the Three Watchers.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis faces a choice between two upgrades to Reumah's Rest. Either would make it a rank three fortification, and the ambitious version would add a flotilla able to intercept barbarian navies in its waters.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the opening in-character exchange refers to "Reumah's Redoubt" on the southern coast, but no opportunity concerns the Redoubt territory.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oranseri would gain the Celesti Lighthouse bastion and garrison, lose its abandoned quality, and be defended from sea attack by Freeborn fleets on guarding voyages.
r.Morrow/Operus: Operus is the site of the proposed Four Points rank two fortification, costing 140 white granite and 280 crowns, with a bastion and a patrolling garrison.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Coursmouth, home of Reumah's Rest, would gain the coastal quality through work on its cliffs and bay. Its White Sails garrison could then move along the coast and the River Couros, or become a full warship flotilla.

The matter will be done.d: The manticore of the Untrod Groves led a procession through Dawn, gathering some fifty nobles, including Earl Valerie de Courcillon. Its backers were called the romantics, the brutal and the sinister; its opponents the romantics, the realists and the ambitious. Realists warned that any monarch other than the Throne would force Dawn out of the Empire. Alyss Retainer secured the Anvil arena for a noble-only grand melee, with the Challenger in Waiting expected to ensure a glorious contest. Emperor Vesna planted her banner and challenged. Her forces won an overwhelming victory. The page notes such a victory ends the matter but gives no surge of national Pride.

n.Dawn: Dawn's nobility split over the manticore's challenge, but the threat of a constitutional crisis passed when Emperor Vesna won overwhelmingly, was crowned Monarch of Dawn and the beast was slain.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: realists warned that Dawn's four armies could not face the Druj's nine or more alone, and the brutal faction promised death to every Druj orc.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: realists questioned whether Holberg's citizens would keep paying taxes to maintain the Castle of Thorns if Dawn left the Empire, and Empress Lisabetta's work for Holberg was cited.

t.Astolat: The Seat of the Sun, the Rose Throne of Astolat, was the prize contested; it went to Emperor Vesna rather than the manticore.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: realists asked whether Holberg's wealthy citizens would still pay to maintain the Castle of Thorns if Dawn left the Empire.
t.Semmerholm: The manticore's procession passed through Semmerholm on its way towards the Crown of Thorns, and one of its leading supporters held estates there.
t.The Barrens: The manticore's challenge and procession began from its seat in the Barrens, where Earl Valerie de Courcillon's knights had been harassing the Karass in the south.
t.Weirwater: The manticore's procession marched through Weirwater, and the story of its challenge spread across Weirwater's moors.

r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Earl Sebastian De Marigny, leading voice of the manticore's romantic supporters, keeps estates in Estmure.
r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: Mentioned in passing: the tale of the challenge spread as far as the sacred walls of Arnet in Ulvenholm.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: Mentioned in passing: the story of the challenge reached the Plains of Teeth at the Mallum's door.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The manticore's procession set out from the Untrod Groves, its seat as self-proclaimed Earl, before it was slain at Anvil.

The poisoned air.d: After the Druj were driven from the Sarangrave and the Senate granted it to Urizen, seers mapped the pivotal pillar in each region. Destroying one would clear that region's miasma. They found none in Bendol, one already removed in the Whisperwood, one in Turan Flats and two each in Thornfen, Bloodwater Marsh and Kroll. Several seers died or were captured. Many survivors swore never to return. The miasma is already poisoning the ritual magic of Urizeni settlers and will worsen unless the pillars fall. Named Imperial officials were tasked with expeditions against overgrown foliage, a poison cauldron, a screaming ghost and two bands of Druj Kallad.

n.Druj: The Druj have lost all hold on the Sarangrave, but their ancient pillars remain to break the will of its people. Two elite Kallad banners, the Kull and the Kri, stayed behind to guard pillars in Turan and Kroll and are blamed for the deaths of many seers.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or vallorn-stricken Imperial citizens choose a painless death, extends into Brocéliande and Therunin.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni who once lived in Spiral compared the Sarangrave to their former home at the worst of the Black Plateau.
n.Urizen: Urizen's seers bore the cost of the survey: some were lost, and many survivors vowed never to return. The nation's settlers already feel the miasma corrupting their ritual magic, and it attacks the very ambition, reason and magic that define them.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: much of the Empire's knowledge of miasma pillars came from Ossium, where the pillars had been hastily and cheaply built.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift reaches into Brocéliande, letting those fallen in vallorn miasma choose dissolution.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the pillars destroyed in Ossium are described as hastily erected affairs, unlike the ancient ones of the Sarangrave.
t.Sarangrave: The territory remains blighted by ancient, deeply rooted miasma pillars that have shaped its land and people for generations. Seers identified the keystone pillars whose destruction would lift the miasma region by region, and Druj Kallad still guard some of them.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: former residents of Spiral likened the Sarangrave to Spiral when the Black Plateau was at its worst.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift extends into Therunin.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Empire first learned about miasma pillars in Zenith, and the Kull are said to have corrupted its Tower of the Fall to unleash the Endless Stalker as the Druj retreated.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: the seers found, unsurprisingly, no keystone pillar in Bendol.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Two keystone pillars lie here. One is shrouded in deadly fumes from an abandoned Druj cauldron, which the Guild Leader of the Apothecaries is tasked with neutralising. The seers who know where the other lies have been captured but might still be rescued.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The Kri banner of Kallad, aided by Spring practitioners, guards two linked pillars here, and the Scribes of Atonaius were among the seers lost investigating them. The Knight-protector of Spring is charged with destroying both pillars.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Two keystone pillars stand in Thornfen. One is choked by semi-sentient strangling foliage that killed two seers and is assigned to the Gardener of Pallas. The other is guarded by a screaming ghost that the High Exorcist must deal with.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The Kull banner of Kallad guards the region's pillar while a Winter coven of ghulai tries to use the Culling Stone regio to curse the territory. The Keeper of the Tower of the Fall is tasked with stopping them both.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Mentioned in passing: the Whisperwood's keystone pillar had already been removed.

Things go awry.d: The regio still worked in every other respect. Covens of the same nation could still cooperate freely, while arcane projections creating personal curses failed for good after the Equinox. The shrouds over the Empire and its neighbours collapsed, and the Key and the Spider now prevented any territory-scale shroud. Vivid star-dreams granted inspiration to dreamers. Rivers of Life had strange effects: a fertility boon in Feroz, blood weeping from Mitwold's Pale Chain, and a sudden woodland in Bregasland. In Redoubt it agitated the Ribbon of Salt, which threatened to devastate the Bay of Catazar. A Night shroud hid Miekarova's Painted Caves, and a Day enchantment brought clarity to Sermersuaq.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their Mallum lands lost their mysterious shrouds, the Salt Flats of Sanath cannot now be shrouded, and the miasma over Druj-claimed land colours visions felt through the Citadel Guard in Sarangrave.
n.Grendel: Grendel-held shores of the Bay of Catazar would be struck by ruinous storms if the Ribbon of Salt erupted, and some at Anvil might think that damage worth inflicting simply to hurt the Grendel.
n.Highguard: The shroud over Casinea and the Imperial regio, broken at the Winter Solstice, proved to be the lynchpin of the wider shrouds, and Necropolis lies on the coast threatened by the Ribbon of Salt.
n.Jotun: The shrouds that had settled over Skallahn, Tromsa, Hordalant, Liathaven and Bregasland disintegrated, and no territory-scale shroud could be raised over these lands during the Spring Equinox.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was among the neighbouring territories whose unexplained shroud collapsed after the Winter Solstice.
n.The Brass Coast: Feroz's farms and the Dhomiro of Afar's Herds were offered a Stallion-touched fertility boon, but the Brass Coast's recovering coastal towns would suffer badly if the Ribbon of Salt erupted.
n.The League: Sarvos and Spiral lie on the Bay of Catazar, and Sarvos would be pounded by Spring storms if the Ribbon of Salt exploded.
n.The Marches: Blood seeped from the soil around the Pale Chain in Mitwold, where Red Walder's heirs were seen taking something from the ground, while a new woodland sprang up in Bregasland and Graven Rock echoed strangely.
n.Thule: The Thule faced a magical mist barring the Painted Caves of Mieriada that they did not create and resent, and which Imperial magicians could extend for a year or make permanent, angering them.
n.Urizen: Magicians channelling ritual magic through the Citadel Guard felt a physical connection to its Urizeni soldiers. Meanwhile Redoubt's agitated Ribbon of Salt threatened disaster, and its senator Thalia of Netherwatch was sent seawater for a mitigating ritual.
n.Varushka: The Painted Caves, special to Varushkans who feel their Ushkan heritage, were hidden by mists under the Lock. Some saw this as passive resistance to Thule occupation that could be extended or made permanent.
n.Wintermark: A Day enchantment over Sermersuaq tore apart the last echoes of the Falconer's influence and brought calm, clarity and encounters with Day heralds to the territory's people.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Ribbon of Salt beneath the bay was erupting roughly every eighteen hours. Any Spring enchantment or curse on Redoubt during the Equinox would unleash storms that cripple fleets and inflict heavy navy casualties across the bay.
t.Bregasland: A brand new woodland rose in a single night between Gravenmarch and the Rushes and Graven Rock echoed with unsettling resonances, possibly linked to Rivers of Life. The territory's earlier shroud also collapsed.
t.Casinea: The potent shroud over Casinea was broken at the Winter Solstice, and now the Key and the Spider, rather than the Lock, glitter in its skies.
t.Feroz: Rivers of Life under the Stallion brought a surge of births and fertility, so farms blessed at the Winter Solstice would yield extra rings. The Dhomiro of Afar was offered a star-metal ritual to permanently increase the Herds' income, though the territory would also face the Ribbon's storms.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun lands whose shroud collapsed and which could not be shrouded again during the Equinox.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: named among neighbouring territories whose unexplained shroud disintegrated after the Winter Solstice.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Bay of Catazar territories that would be struck by storms if the Ribbon of Salt erupted.
t.Mareave: Mareave would be battered by Spring storms if the Ribbon of Salt exploded, with Beoraidh among the places named as being pounded.
t.Miekarova: The Painted Caves in ceded Mieriada were hidden by a magnitude 30 Night shroud that the Thule did not cast. Imperial magicians invoking the Lock could extend it for a year or make it permanent.
t.Mitwold: Blood-like liquid seeped from old battlefields, and the Pale Chain wept blood under the Key, where Jyll Longleys, Bill of Beatsdown and Cobb were seen pulling something from the ground: an ill omen for the warzone.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Bay of Catazar territories threatened by storms should the Ribbon of Salt erupt.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: almost all of Otkodov had been shrouded before the shrouds collapsed, and its orcs are referred to in the context of resistance in Miekarova.
t.Redoubt: Rivers of Life promised fine harvests but agitated the Ribbon of Salt under the Mountain, Stork and Wanderer. Any Spring enchantment or curse on Redoubt would cause disaster unless a precise Regrow the Land's Heart invoking the Fountain bled off its power.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the territories over which no shroud could be created during the Spring Equinox.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard were stationed there, colouring rituals channelled through them with phantoms of marsh and battle, and Rivers of Life caused chaos at the Tower of the Skink.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was named among the places that Spring storms would pound if the Ribbon of Salt exploded across the Bay of Catazar.
t.Sermersuaq: A Day enchantment unravelled the Falconer's lingering corruption, dimmed the Claw, and filled the territory with clarity, wellbeing and gentle encounters with Day heralds. Its people felt Day magic more keenly as a result.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun lands whose shroud collapsed and which could not be shrouded during the Equinox.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: listed among the Bay of Catazar territories at risk of storms if the Ribbon of Salt erupted.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: named among the neighbouring territories whose unexplained shroud disintegrated after the Winter Solstice.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: listed among Jotun lands whose shroud collapsed and which could not be shrouded during the Equinox.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: A brand new woodland erupted overnight on Gravenmarch's border with the Rushes, amid speculation that it is linked to Rivers of Life and to strange resonances in Graven Rock.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The sudden new woodland rose on the Rushes' border with Gravenmarch, prompting landskeepers to suggest divination and mummers to plan dramatisations of a moving forest.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Beoraidh was named among the places that devastating Spring storms would pound if the Ribbon of Salt exploded.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The Painted Caves of Mieriada, some holding Night regio, were sealed off by mists that led travellers astray and could be extended for a year or made permanent by invoking the Lock.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly and is attached through Redoubt, where the agitated Ribbon of Salt threatened the territory's coast.

Towards a common good.d: Paulk Thornweaver won the patronage of the Beurteilung at the Winter Solstice for twenty-six thrones. Gelberg's team proposed that Highborn generals on defensive orders could send officers and experts to aid Commonwealth counterparts in return for gifts, or send key figures from a newly raised army to Commonwealth war colleges for six months. Henrik Hexenjäger asked Highguard to build a Hexenjäger Academy, creating the national title of Bursar of the Hexenjäger. The Synod could also explicitly rule that preaching the Common Good was not heresy, though Naomi of Virtue's Rest warned this risked weakening the faith. Gelberg announced he would complete one final assignment and return home shortly before the Summer Solstice 388YE.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the only link is Naomi of Virtue's Rest saying she had been engaged with matters in the Sarangrave, which they held.
n.Highguard: Highborn generals were offered the chance to aid the Commonwealth or train a new army there, and the nation could commission the Hexenjäger Academy in any Highborn region to create the Bursar of the Hexenjäger, appointed by Tally of the Votes or the National Assembly. Naomi of Virtue's Rest cautioned the Synod against permitting the Common Good to spread.

t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Naomi of Virtue's Rest explained she had not fully appraised the matter because she had been engaged with matters in the Sarangrave.

Voice irresistable.d: Runa proposed a private Summer meeting with Ambassador Kindra. Thania of the Blackstaff's offer of Icy Crag ritual texts still stands. Orobus's offer of 12 rings of ilium for weirwood saplings lapses at the end of the Equinox. Fraynir offered a Senate appraisal of the Thule Winter wards in Sküld, available until the Summer Solstice, if the Conclave sanctions sharing Dreadful Ending. Runa objected to Imperial rituals in Ossium, Sermersuaq and Miekarova, threatening to charge the Empire mana if another shroud covers Miechernya's Painted Caves. Hinodir warned against meddling with the constellations. The Thule claimed victory in Ulnak and asked the High Exorcist for help against ghosts. A joint Varushkan–Thule hunt for face-peelers succeeded.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as one of the nations sending food shipments north to Otkodov under the peace.
n.Druj: The Thule marched east out of Ossium and claim victory in their initial conquest of the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak, aided by Imperial mercenary captains, and they invite Imperial armies to join under Tathenon's strategy.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named. Their territory of Skarsind appears only through Crow's Ridge, listed among the regions that are politically Thule but still subject to Imperial magic cast on the territory.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is named as one of the nations shipping food north to Otkodov under the peace treaties.
n.Thule: Otkodov installed Runa as its new ambassador to the Empire. It pressed the Empire on vallorn wards, ritual texts and weirwood, and warned against rituals touching its people. It also claimed victory in its push into the Forest of Ulnak.
n.Varushka: Many Varushkan captains joined the Thule Claws of the Dragon in successfully rooting out face-peelers in Karsk and Ossium. Runa protested the Rot-empowered enchantment on Ossium and the shroud over Miechernya's Painted Caves.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Kindra Surefoot serves as the Empire's ambassador to the Thule. The Sky and Ice enchantment on Sermersuaq drew little Thule concern, and Runa noted that the Thule committed three armies to Sermersuaq's liberation.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The Thule began a systematic conquest of the Forest of Ulnak and claimed victory, but ghosts in the forest have cost them valuable materials, which they have asked the Empire's High Exorcist to help recover.
t.Karsk: Varushkan captains and the Claws of the Dragon hunted the trudniki face-peelers across Karsk, briefly disrupting draughir communities, and the effort appears to have succeeded.
t.Miekarova: The ambassadorial offices in Miekarova were readied for Runa, and Thania of the Blackstaff keeps her ritual text offer open while she remains there. An Imperial shroud over the Painted Caves drew a firm Thule protest.
t.Ossium: The Rot lord-empowered Spring enchantment brought heralds and ruin to the Thule regions of Ossium, prompting Runa to call for a ritual protocol. Orobus seeks weirwood saplings to plant there, and face-peelers were hunted there too.
t.Otkodov: The Thule are building permanent Winter-warded camps against the vallorn in Sküld, and the Empire may appraise them. Imperial astronomantic disorder spread magical shrouds over Verthandi, Urdr and Sküld.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the ghosts troubling the Thule in Ulnak are described as the same kind as those afflicting the Sarangrave orcs.
t.Sermersuaq: An Imperial ritual aligned Sermersuaq with the realm of Sky and Ice, helping clear corruption from the Dragon's Talon but letting Day heralds into the Silver Peaks. The Dragons were largely unconcerned.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind appears only through Crow's Ridge, listed among Thule-held regions that remain part of their Imperial territory for magical purposes.
t.Verthandi: Warlocks found Verthandi blanketed by a magical shroud, which Hinodir identified as a spill-over of the Empire's constellation disorder rather than cover for an attack.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Mentioned in passing: Krevsaty is listed among the regions that are politically part of Otkodov but still subject to Imperial magic laid on Karsk.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: An Imperial shroud made the Painted Caves of Miechernya unreachable, which Runa called unacceptable under the treaty. If it recurs, Hinodir will remove it and the Empire must pay the mana.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The Thule ambassadorial offices in Mieriada were hurriedly prepared for the new ambassador, Runa.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Rot-empowered heralds and magic caused ruin in the Bonewood. Orobus wants weirwood saplings that remember the vallorn to share their experiences with its trees.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Rot lord-empowered enchantment on Ossium caused consternation and some ruin in the Webwood, though warlocks dealt with the heralds.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Fraynir is building warded camps around the vallorn of Stathas surrounding Emrys in Sküld and offers the Empire an appraisal of them. Sküld was also shrouded by the Empire's star-related disorder.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Sky and Ice alignment let Day heralds enter the Silver Peaks unbidden; Thule warlocks dealt with them at some cost in time.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Mentioned in passing: Crow's Ridge is listed among Thule-held regions that remain within Skarsind under the Law of Dominion.

Weaving tangled nets.d: The Commonwealth questioned the Liberty Pact's future and imposed a -1 trade penalty at Volkavaar, Leerdam and newly opened Murolosch over Imperial trade at Radosmo. It also pressed for news of its magicians trapped in the Lyceum. The Granite Pillar, Rod and Shield and Golden Pyramid aided the Commonwealth and earned gifts of Soldier's Booze, Hero Stones and war ring schema. In Jarm, the Celestial Arch laid groundwork for a possible ceasefire summit, the Shuttered Lantern gathered intelligence, and the Sevenfold Path met the Convocation of Virtue. The Silver Chalice saved hundreds in Lantir, though some returned cursed. Containment failed, and the Senate could commission an appraisal to find further ways to help.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean Plenum suggested to the Jarmish that Cold Sun might be related to Dawn and that Jarm might question the Empire about it.
n.Highguard: Thaumiel of Steeplechase Toll, Highguard's Ambassador to Jarm, was received briefly by Lord-Magister Trescher. Veterans of the Highborn army the Granite Pillar advised the Commonwealth generals and earned a seasonal gift of Soldier's Booze for their general.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Commonwealth soldiers are recalled as having fought and died alongside the Freeborn in the fall of Siroc.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: some members of Jarm's Convocation of Virtue first encountered the Way while visiting Sarvos on mercantile business.
n.Wintermark: Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark, as Ambassador to the Commonwealth, faced scepticism over the Radosmo trade and pointed questions about the Lyceum captives. Lofyn Bloodcloak's Cold Sun experience was welcomed, and cursed Silver Chalice members planned to meet at the Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar's orders had it hold a strategic defence of Astolat to resupply while sending officers to advise the Commonwealth.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Siroc is recalled as a battle where Commonwealth soldiers fought and died alongside the Freeborn.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: contact with Sarcophan pilgrims three generations ago is listed among the origins of Jarm's Convocation of Virtue.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: conversations held while visiting Sarvos on mercantile matters are cited as one way some Jarmish came to the Way.

Where the slow river flows.d: The original Jotun host withdrew west, leaving the Corazón, Escuta and Hierro in Mitwold. The Drakes, Tusks, Golden Sun, Valiant Pegasus, Green Shield and the Forte Fidelis garrison held a firm defensive line. At Wayford the Lasambrians were ambushed crossing the Meade. Wild Spring magic, linked to the Green Willow and the Rivers of Life curse, raised healing geysers that turned the fight into a brutal drowning melee until both sides withdrew. Barbarian casualties were roughly three times Imperial losses. The Corazón looted Meade and Wayford's football trophies. Stephen of Sarcombe was not seen, but he armed the heirs of Red Walder, whose raids brought Banditry to the Meadows and both Downs.

n.Dawn: Lord Daemon Mortére's Golden Sun held the line in Mitwold beside the Drakes and Dawnish knights joined the Wayford ambush. The Golden Sun also helped drive off the heirs of Red Walder when they attacked baggage trains and refugees.
n.Jotun: The Lasambrian-Jotun armies lost the Meadows and suffered heavy casualties at Wayford, yet still held Meade March and Oddmire and carried off much plunder. The Jarl-of-Jarls and many champions reportedly view Stephen of Sarcombe as a liability.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: many Lasambrians at Wayford were veterans of the plains of Segura and the hills of Kahraman, and their struggles on Segura's flat ground are recalled.
n.The Marches: Marcher armies, militia and the Forte Fidelis garrison defended Mitwold and reclaimed the Meadows, but Meade and Oddmire stayed in Jotun hands. Jim Moor's murder dented morale, and the heirs of Red Walder now raid the Marchers' own lands.
n.Wintermark: The Green Shield under Iron Osric fought with honour and led the only Imperial offensive, driving the Lasambrians from the Meadows and gaining a tenth of the way towards liberating Meade March. Wintermark heroes also fought among the Imperial captains.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched out of Bregasland to reach Mitwold, and the Green Shield aimed to drive the Jotun west towards it.
t.Fjorknae: The Lasambrians plan to ship their Meade plunder over the Sea of Snow to hire a large warband of Fjorknae orcs unless Imperial heroes recover it.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: some Lasambrian soldiers at Wayford were veterans of fighting in the hills of Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the recent assault on Kierheim is cited as exposing a vulnerability that drew the western Jotun's interest.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was the main battleground: the Empire reclaimed the Meadows and held both Downs, while Meade March and Oddmire remained under Jotun control and were plundered. Healing Spring rains promise a bumper harvest, but bandits backed by Stephen of Sarcombe now trouble the territory.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Green March, Alderly and the Chalkdowns, and Imperial efforts to bolster Marcher Pride and Loyalty had focused partly on the Mournwold.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Corazón are eager to return to Reinos with their loot, news comes of the Iron Confederacy marching into Chaveiro, and the jarl holding the Beater Cup hails from Corghosa.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrians intend to ship their plunder across the Sea of Snow to entice the Fjorknae orcs.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Lasambrian veterans of Segura's plains fought at Wayford, and their weakness on Segura's flat ground is cited.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: much of the metal in a Jotun supply cache in Meade March likely came from the mines of Skallahn.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the plunder sled is built like those used by the natives of Tromsa.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: the page cites the recent assault on Kierheim as having drawn the interest of the western Jotun.
r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: The Imperial armies gathered at the Golden Downs, which stayed in Imperial hands, but the region gained Banditry as Red Walder's heirs raided there.
r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: The Maiden Downs remained under Imperial control but gained Banditry because of raids by the heirs of Red Walder.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: Meade March, including the city of Meade, stayed in Jotun hands and was thoroughly looted by the Corazón, though the Green Shield got a tenth of the way to liberating it. Heroes have the chance to fight at Meade Meadow to recover the stolen treasure, the Beater Cup and a healing spring.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Oddmire remained under Lasambrian-Jotun control and was among the places the Corazón plundered.
r.Mitwold/The Meadows: The Meadows saw the bloody Battle of Wayford and were fully reclaimed by the Empire, though the Corazón looted Wayford and the region gained Banditry from Red Walder's heirs.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes passed through the outskirts of Alderly on their way to Mitwold.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes crossed the Chalkdowns en route to the Golden Downs.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes marched through Green March out of Bregasland.
r.Reinos/Chaveiro: Mentioned in passing: news of the Iron Confederacy marching into Chaveiro spurred the Corazón to flee home with their loot.
r.Reinos/Corghosa: Mentioned in passing: Aitana Redondo, the jarl holding the stolen Beater Cup, comes from the hills of Corghosa.

Who counts the path untaken?.d: The Imperial feint on Kierheim drew Jotun armies back across the Kongegőr, but Imperial forces had already withdrawn, and the Jotun now know the bridge is vulnerable. Jarl Igya Olgafsdottir has called a hetjuveisla at Gull's Isle Hall, with Ingrid Talon-of-the-Mark responsible for engaging. The smidr Harald Fourforge wishes to discuss limits on magic in war and asks Vossk to choose attendees. After the Loyalty Assembly's writ and Wintermark's statement against evangelism, the Jotun responded warmly to a sample Peerless Kinship aura. A General Assembly mandate is proposed to consecrate a shrine, helped by a Sentinel Gate conjunction at the Summer Solstice.

n.Jotun: The Jotun armies retook Skallahn and guarded the Kongegőr, and their jarls are preparing to feast and negotiate with Imperial leaders at the hetjuveisla. Many ghodi and warriors were also deeply moved by the Loyalty aura.
n.The Marches: A major Jotun force was pulled away from the fighting in the Marches to defend the north, but enough remains to keep threatening Mitwold and Bregasland.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark has long had a close, if warlike, relationship with the Jotun. Its National Assembly's statement of principle reassured the Jotun that the Gull Isle Meeting Place would not be used for preaching.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland remains conquered by the Jotun, who have kept enough force in the south to go on threatening it.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is not named on the page, which deals with the wider Jotun war and the Meeting Place on Gull Isle.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is listed among the lands the Jotun have conquered, which they call Ashvale.
t.Mitwold: The Jotun invasion of Mitwold continues; although forces were drawn north, the orcs left enough behind to keep threatening it.
t.Skallahn: The land the Empire had claimed in Skallahn was retaken without real resistance after the Imperial retreat from Kierheim. The Jotun now recognise that the Kongegőr bridge is under threat.
t.Tromsa: The hetjuveisla being held at Gull's Isle Hall is a Tromsdalen tradition of hospitality that lets feuding warbands negotiate in good faith.

r.Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor: Jarl Ottesen of Ulfrsmoor was impressed when the murder of her thralls was solved, and she recommended the smidr Harald Fourforge to attend the hetjuveisla.
r.Tromsa/Tromsdalen: The hetjuveisla is a Tromsdalen custom: both sides bring food, drink and bards, and a day must pass after the feast before violence resumes.

Wide azure skies.d: The Grendel brought down the Blood River Colossi and Fleisardh's cliffs, opening the coast to the Golden Winds and Shamal navies. These landed the Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Hamsin, the last backed by Asavean mercenaries paid by the Plenum. Outnumbered despite Day magic, ice giants of the Isjättens Väggar, Rucraic's Redoubt with the Ramparts of Ashlar and Skouran battle-engineers, the Imperial armies retreated and made a bloody stand in Clisearn. Local orcs began quietly supporting the defenders, and amethyst-sailed Grendel ships were sighted approaching. A Sentinel Gate opportunity at Ohwinn Scour offered chances to summon Iskanders Donjon, negotiate with or kill Scutt-Tadhg, rescue the Tholdie Rotary, kill Evdokia, and curse Fergus Konnaugh.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the toppling of the Colossi is said to be strategy rather than vandalism, since 'the Grendel are not the Druj'.
n.Grendel: Grendel forces retook Fleisardh with five armies and two navies, aided by Asavean mercenaries, and pressed halfway into Clisearn, though the Black Eels' indiscriminate raiding alienated local orcs.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun and Seventh Wave lost Fleisardh but held stubbornly in Clisearn, winning quiet support and new recruits among Mareave's orcs, with opportunities to bind the Clisearn families to them.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks left Mareave for Spiral before the fighting.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Winds and Shamal navies sailed south from Redoubt to join the attack on Mareave.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Brine Turtle negotiator Scutt-Tadhg's role is likened to that of a Wintermark mediator.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Spring storm clouds gathered above the bay as Winter faded.
t.Mareave: The Empire lost its hold on Fleisardh and the Grendel are halfway to conquering Clisearn, with both sides still locked in fighting as more Grendel ships approach.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel Golden Winds and Shamal navies set sail from Redoubt to reinforce Fleisardh.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks left Mareave bound for Spiral.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies sailed through Beoraidh's waters on their way to Fleisardh.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: The Grendel pushed halfway into Clisearn, held back largely by the Isjättens Väggar, while local families began giving provisions to Imperial soldiers and the three families faced pressure to choose a side.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Orcs of Eoradal came to watch the enchanted defenders of Rucraic's Redoubt, and a few would-be warriors quietly asked the Sannite about the Unshackled and the Empire.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Grendel ritual magic collapsed the Blood River Colossi and the coastal cliffs, poisoning the shore, and the Grendel drove the Imperial armies out of the region entirely.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Mentioned in passing: Grendel ships sailed past its cliffs, and its orcs came to view the sigils of Rucraic's Redoubt.
r.Mareave/Nadir: A frozen citadel rose in Nadir to support the Empire, and some local orcs came to view Rucraic's Redoubt and asked about joining the Unshackled.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies sailed past the cliffs of Sinfoyard on their way south.

Wise and measured.d: The Scions of Cavan were executed or fined into destitution after a lengthy trial, and Axos handed fugitive Disciples of Sulemaine back to Imperial magistrates. Navarr traders remain viewed with suspicion in Issyk and Kantor, though the Grand Council does not endorse closing those ports to them. Mistress Isephenia began studying the vallorn at the Great Library of Hacynian. Axos withdrew its queries about the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy. It insisted the orcs of Thornfen would be evicted and left to the Empire. The Civil Service will raise a motion confirming the Thornfen treaty, which Urizen may veto. Fintan Nighthaven's body was returned to Axos, the Rebuker of the Unwanted will be handed back at the Summer Solstice, and Pathfinder Brog's request for library access was declined.

n.Druj: The Druj grip over the Mallum is described as broken after the Empire captured Thornfen, and a Druj raid on the Shield of Ipotavo was intercepted, recovering the Axou relic the Rebuker of the Unwanted.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: in the opening fiction an Axou grandfather urges his granddaughter to study with a tutor at the House of Spirits and train in Highguard.
n.Navarr: Navarr traders are still unwelcome in Issyk and Kantor, the Scions of Cavan's plea to the Navarr went unanswered, and Fintan Nighthaven's remains were returned to Axos in line with his family's wishes.
n.The League: Axos withdrew its queries about the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy, accepting the Empire's concerns about military security, though an international college of war might be discussed later.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Axou scholars at the Great Library are reviewing vallorn research gathered from Imperial and Thule sources.
n.Urizen: The Urizen assembly may veto the Senate's administrative motion confirming the treaty, as it would concede a region under Urizen control to Axos.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's 'Shacklebreaker' Thanmir Hrafnar, Imperial Ambassador to Axos, was credited with heading off a backlash over the Scions of Cavan and holds the recovered Rebuker of the Unwanted pending its return.

t.Sarangrave: With Thornfen captured, the treaty intends to cede Thornfen, the Tower of the Skink and Sephals to Axos, which plans a new citadel in Sarangrave, subject to a Senate motion.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven's remains were carried to Crown Quay and loaded onto a black-sailed Axou ship.

r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Captured by the Empire with the help of the Axou army of Ipotavo, Thornfen is promised to Axos, which says it will evict the orcs living there and leave their fate to the Empire.

Your hand in mine.d: The Conscience of the Senate's motion sent Naomi to the rebels of Nesustak Forest. Three approaches, one to each sept, were driven off at bow-point, so she ruled out any commission, motion or judgement for now. Instead she found a conjunction at 14:00 on Sunday leading five citizens to the rebels' armed camp near the Bloodwater Marsh. She offered seven pieces of guidance, urged the envoys to go unarmed and aim only for further talks, and recommended Ser Guy of the Twisted Rose, Fausta Ankarien and Aspar. She advised against the Throne going. The Senate must choose the envoys. Unless something is done, the vallorn will destroy the rebels within three months.

n.Druj: The rebels threw off Druj rule and fear the Druj above all, while the vallorn the Druj unleashed in Sarangrave threatens to wipe them out. A failed meeting would hand the Druj more propaganda against the Empire among the septs still in Ulnak and Sanath.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page; its only connection is its share in holding Sarangrave, the territory the rebels claim.

t.Sarangrave: The rebel septs want Sarangrave for themselves and refuse to talk to the Empire. The one chance at diplomacy is a single meeting at their camp, while the Druj-unleashed vallorn closes in on them.

r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: The Sentinel Gate conjunction opens on the edge of the Bloodwater Marsh, close to the rebels' main camp. The Bloodwater Spears, one of the two leading rebel septs, are among those the envoys must understand.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Nesustak rebels drove off Naomi's envoys but were saved from the Druj by the Gryphon's Pride. If nothing is done, the vallorn will obliterate them within three months.
